endorsements.title: Adoption of AI in Healthcare Delivery Systems: Early Applications and Impacts
endorsements.quote: Should we be intentional about driving adoption — or let interest drive adoption?

endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: The report content should clearly communicate the association between the genetic variants identified for the patient and the suggested treatment options.

endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Accessibility: Is the AI's output presented in a way that is comprehensible and usable for the clinicians or patients receiving the information?

endorsements.title: Principles for augmented intelligence development, deployment, and use
endorsements.quote: Nevertheless, as NIST notes, meaningful transparency should provide access to appropriate levels of information based on the stage of the AI lifecycle and tailored to the role or knowledge of individuals interacting with or using the AI system.

endorsements.title: Advancing Global Nursing Policy: AI-Driven Health Literacy Innovations for Migrant Domestic Workers
endorsements.quote: Trained at the intersection of clinical care and information systems, they can ensure that chatbots and decision‐support tools use plain language consistent with health literacy principles, incorporate appropriate clinical safeguards, and maintain transparent privacy controls (Booth et al. 2021 ).

endorsements.title: Decoding the "black-box": explainable artificial intelligence towards trustworthy advancement in respiratory medicine
endorsements.quote: Patient-facing XAI interfaces should prioritise health literacy, using clear visualisations and avoiding technical jargon while maintaining accuracy.

endorsements.title: Participatory Digital Twins for Chronic Care: From Predictive Models to Shared Sensemaking
endorsements.quote: Therefore, PDTs should incorporate translation mechanisms, potentially including GenAI-mediated dialogue, that allow users to ask questions, request clarification, and explore alternatives in plain language.

evidence.title: Patient-centric radiology: Utilising large language models (LLMs) to improve patient communication and education
evidence.outcome: Patient comprehension with formal report plus LLM-simplified report versus formal only
evidence.effect: 95% reported understanding >50% with simplified report vs 46% without (rank biserial correlation 0.67, p<0.001); simplified reports at 5th-9th grade vs 11th-13th grade for formal
evidence.quote: Patients with both reports demonstrated a significantly greater comprehension level, with 95% reporting an understanding level greater than 50%, compared with 46% without the simplified report (rank biserial correlation = 0.67, p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Provision of Radiology Reports Simplified With Large Language Models to Patients With Cancer: Impact on Patient Satisfaction
evidence.outcome: Patient knowledge, confidence, and understanding with simplified vs original CT report impressions
evidence.effect: Simplified report group had significantly better knowledge of primary site and disease extent and higher confidence and understanding (P < .05 for all).
evidence.quote: In phase II, simplified report group patients demonstrated significantly better knowledge of primary site and extent of their disease as well as showed significantly higher confidence and understanding of the report (P < .05 for all).

evidence.title: Evaluation of AI Summaries on Interdisciplinary Understanding of Ophthalmology Notes
evidence.outcome: Clinician understanding, satisfaction, clarity and readability of notes with vs without LLM plain language summary
evidence.effect: Diagnostic understanding +9.0 percentage points (95% CI 0.3-18.2); note detail satisfaction +21.5 points; explanation clarity +23.0 points; Flesch Reading Ease 51.8 vs 43.6.
evidence.quote: Nonophthalmology clinicians and professionals reported enhanced diagnostic understanding (percentage point increase, 9.0; 95% CI, 0.3-18.2; P = .01), increased note detail satisfaction (percentage point increase, 21.5; 95% CI, 11.4-31.5; P < .001), and improved explanation clarity (percentage point increase, 23.0; 95% CI, 12.0-33.1; P < .001) for notes containing a PLS.
evidence.sample_unit: ophthalmologist review responses on LLM-generated plain language summaries (plus 362 nonophthalmology respondents preferring PLS)

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence Large Language Models Improve Patient Comprehension of Radiologist Magnetic Resonance Imaging Reports
evidence.venue: Arthroscopy : the journal of arthroscopic & related surgery : official publication of the Arthroscopy Association of North America and the International Arthroscopy Association
evidence.outcome: Patient comprehension quiz score for AI plain-language MRI report versus standard radiologist report
evidence.effect: AI group scored 20% higher than standard MRI group on comprehension quiz (74.7% vs 54.7%, P < .001); 87.5% preferred AI translation; clarity 4.5 vs 2.2 of 5.
evidence.quote: Patients in the AI group scored 20% higher than those in the standard MRI group on the comprehension quiz (74.7% vs 54.7%, P < .001).

evidence.title: A Prospective Controlled Trial of Large Language Model-based Simplification of Oncologic CT Reports for Patients with Cancer
evidence.outcome: Patient comprehension, cognitive workload, perceived usefulness, reading time and readability of simplified versus standard CT reports
evidence.effect: Simplified reports gave lower cognitive workload (adjusted OR 0.18), better comprehension (adjusted OR 13.28) and better perceived usefulness (adjusted OR 5.46). Median reading time fell from 7 to 2 minutes. Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level was 8.89 vs 13.69.
evidence.quote: LLM simplification of oncologic CT reports improved patient comprehension and reduced reading burden.

evidence.title: Embedding LLMs in the patient portal to summarize acute minor illness information: a three-arm experimental study
evidence.outcome: Patient comprehension of acute minor illness information at Day 14 with vs without LLM plain-language summaries
evidence.effect: Comprehension at Day 14 was higher with LLM summaries (Claude M=81.4, GPT-5.1 M=79.6) than control (M=63.2); F(2,169)=47.34, p<0.001, partial η2=0.36.
evidence.quote: LLM-embedded patient portal summaries significantly improved comprehension of acute minor illnesses and reduced unnecessary healthcare utilization in a primary care setting.

evidence.title: AI-generated patient-friendly discharge summaries to empower patients
evidence.outcome: Patient self-reported understanding after reading AI-generated plain-language discharge summary
evidence.effect: 90% (18/20) reported better understanding after reading the summary, including those who initially felt well-informed; 90% found it more helpful than discharge consultations.
evidence.quote: Among hospitalized patients recruited at two departments in our tertiary care hospital (n=20), most (90%) reported better understanding after reading the AI-generated summary, including those who initially felt well-informed.

evidence.title: Enhancing Doctor-Patient Communication Using Large Language Models for Pathology Report Interpretation
evidence.outcome: Patient understanding score and doctor-patient communication time with plain-language AI-interpreted pathology reports versus original reports
evidence.effect: Patient understanding rose from 5.23 to 7.98 points (P<0.001); communication time fell over 70%, from 35 to 10 minutes (P<0.001) with interpretive pathology reports.
evidence.quote: Among 698 pathology reports analyzed, the interpretation through LLMs significantly improved readability and patient understanding.

evidence.title: AI-driven simplification of surgical reports in gynecologic oncology: A potential tool for patient education
evidence.outcome: Patient understanding of GPT-4 simplified versus original surgical reports
evidence.effect: Simplified reports significantly improved patients' understanding, particularly of the procedure, its outcome, and potential risks.
evidence.quote: The simplified surgical reports generated by GPT-4 significantly improved our patients' understanding, particularly with regard to the surgical procedure, its outcome, and potential risks.

evidence.title: A Guideline-Concordant Chatbot Framework for Structured Colorectal Cancer Screening: Multistage Feasibility Study
evidence.outcome: Personalization and clarity after adding simplified language and standardized formatting (V3 vs V2)
evidence.effect: V3 improved personalization and clarity (adjusted P=.02) and safety and fairness (adjusted P<.001) vs V2; other dimensions not significant.
evidence.quote: Compared with prompt V2, prompt V3 demonstrated statistically significant improvements only in personalization and clarity (adjusted P =.02) and safety and fairness (adjusted P <.001), whereas differences in the remaining dimensions did not reach statistical significance (adjusted P >.05).

evidence.title: Medical Knowledge Simplification for Patients in the Era of LLMs: A Case Study on Diabetes
evidence.outcome: Reading level (FKGL) of LLM-simplified diabetes responses and user satisfaction
evidence.effect: MediClear consistently reduced reading level of generated responses to the recommended patient literacy range, with high user satisfaction and willingness for future use (10 participants).
evidence.quote: Results show that MediClear consistently reduces the reading level of generated responses to the recommended patient literacy range while achieving high user satisfaction and willingness for future use.

evidence.title: GPT-4 Enhances Readability of Online Patient Materials for Cardiac Amyloidosis
evidence.outcome: Readability of simplified patient education materials
evidence.effect: Median FKGL decreased from 10.9 to 7.8; 14/86 (16.3%) reached 6th-grade level.
evidence.quote: In comparison, GPT-4 revised PEMs reduced the median FKGL to 7.8 (seventh grade; IQR: 7.0, 8.8, p<0.001), with 14/86 (16.3%) achieving at least a 6th-grade reading level.

evidence.title: Validation of an AI-powered mobile application for personalizing medical note explanations
evidence.outcome: Readability of AI-simplified medical notes versus original notes (FKGL, Flesch Reading Ease, Gunning Fog)
evidence.effect: FKGL decreased 2.96 levels (10.57→7.61); Flesch Reading Ease rose 31.9 points (37.7→69.6); Gunning Fog fell 4.09 points (14.5→10.4); child 4.25 grade reduction vs adult 1.80.
evidence.quote: AI-generated explanations showed significant readability improvements: mean Flesch–Kincaid Grade Level decreased by 2.96 levels (10.57→7.61), Flesch Reading Ease increased by 31.9 points (37.7→69.6), and Gunning Fog Index decreased by 4.09 points (14.5→10.4).
evidence.sample_unit: AI-generated outputs (plus 15 healthcare professionals and 54 patients)

evidence.title: Improving Doctor-Patient Communication Using Large Language Models - Results from an Experimental Study
evidence.outcome: Comprehension and subjective understanding of original vs GPT-4 plain-language translated medical notes
evidence.effect: Translated notes yielded higher objective comprehension scores, greater subjective understanding, higher perceived empathy, and reduced mental effort and negative emotions; reading times did not differ.
evidence.quote: LLM translation of medical notes significantly improved both objective and subjective patient understanding.

evidence.title: Comparative Readability of Large Language Models Responses to Male Infertility Questions: Impact of Contextual Prompting
evidence.outcome: Change in readability with contextual lay-patient prompting versus no context
evidence.effect: Readability improved across all models after prompting; Grok best (FRE 69.71±6.09; SMOG 9.96±1.04).
evidence.quote: After prompting, Grok generated the most readable responses (mean FRE 69.71±6.09; mean SMOG 9.96±1.04), and readability improved across all models.
evidence.sample_unit: FAQs on male infertility submitted to each of five LLMs under two prompting conditions

evidence.title: Using GPT-4 to Automate the Generation of Lay Summaries for Cancer Publications
evidence.outcome: patient-perceived clarity and usefulness
evidence.effect: All five patient partners said summaries would help decide whether to join studies and feel more informed.
evidence.quote: All patient partners said these summaries would help them decide whether to join research studies and feel more informed about how their contributions matter.

evidence.title: The Illusion of Understanding: A Randomized Controlled Trial of LLM-Generated Lay Summaries of Brain MRI Reports
evidence.outcome: Objective patient comprehension of brain MRI reports with vs without LLM lay summary
evidence.effect: Objective comprehension did not differ (58.3% vs 59.4%; OR 0.97; 95% CI 0.90–1.06; P = .54); satisfaction and subjective comprehension improved; normal reports worsened (72.5% vs 76.6%).
evidence.quote: Objective comprehension did not differ between arms (58.3% vs 59.4%; odds ratio (OR) 0.97; 95% CI: 0.90–1.06; P = .54).

evidence.title: Large Language Model Responses to Patient Questions About Return to Activities of Daily Living After Knee Arthroplasty: A Multidimensional Evaluation Before and After Plain-Language Prompting
evidence.outcome: Effect of a plain-language prompt on readability, understandability, completeness and treatment-information quality of LLM responses
evidence.effect: Understandability improved (F(1,11)=55.633, P<0.001) and readability increased for all models; DISCERN total fell 11.58 (ChatGPT) and 11.00 (Claude); completeness fell for ChatGPT and Claude; actionability stayed 60%.
evidence.quote: Simplification improved readability and understandability but could reduce completeness and treatment-information quality.
evidence.sample_unit: LLM responses (12 questions x 3 models x 2 prompt stages)

evidence.title: GPT-4 Improves Readability of Institutional Heart Failure Patient Education Materials: An Observational Study
evidence.outcome: Readability and accuracy of GPT-4 plain-language revision of patient education materials
evidence.effect: Median grade level fell from 10th to 7th (p<0.001); PEMs below 6th grade rose from 9.1% to 23.1%; none rated less accurate or comprehensive by cardiologist.
evidence.quote: No GPT-4 revised PEMs were graded as less accurate or less comprehensive compared to institutional PEMs.

evidence.title: Simplifying cardiology research abstracts: assessing ChatGPT’s readability and comprehensibility for non-medical audiences
evidence.outcome: readability of simplified abstracts
evidence.effect: Improved from college graduate level to 8th-9th grade level (p<0.001), but not the requested 5th-grade level.
evidence.quote: The simplification significantly reduced word and character counts (p<0.0001) and improved readability from a college graduate level to an 8th-9th grade level (p<0.001).

evidence.title: The Effects of a Health Care Chatbot's Complexity and Persona on User Trust, Perceived Usability, and Effectiveness: Mixed Methods Study
evidence.outcome: Knowledge-test improvement after chatbot use
evidence.effect: Technical language outperformed nontechnical: OR 2.73 (95% CI 1.05-7.41; P=.04) for high effectiveness.
evidence.quote: Analysis of 71 participants found that participants who received technical language responses were significantly more likely to be in the high effectiveness group, which had higher improvements in test scores (odds ratio [OR] 2.73, 95% CI 1.05-7.41; P=.04).

evidence.title: Simplifying radiologic reports with natural language processing: a novel approach using ChatGPT in enhancing patient understanding of MRI results
evidence.venue: Archives of orthopaedic and trauma surgery
evidence.outcome: Patient-rated comprehensibility of ChatGPT-simplified MRI reports by report complexity
evidence.effect: Simplicity of word choice and sentence structure rated "Agree" on average; patients better at knowing what the text was about (p = 0.001) and drawing correct conclusions (p = 0.013829) the more simplified the report.
evidence.quote: Participants reported being significantly better at knowing what the text was about (p = 0.001) and drawing the correct conclusions the more simplified the report of findings was (p = 0.013829).

evidence.title: Feasibility and acceptability of ChatGPT generated radiology report summaries for cancer patients
evidence.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid grade level of full MRI reports versus ChatGPT plain-language summaries
evidence.effect: Median FK score fell from 9.6 for full MRI reports to 5.0 for summarized reports (p < 0.05).
evidence.quote: The median FK score for the full MRI reports and summarized reports was 9.6 vs. 5.0, (p < 0.05), respectively.
evidence.sample_unit: ChatGPT-summarized MRI reports (from 5 full reports), rated by 12 radiation oncologists

evidence.title: Evaluating the Use of ChatGPT to Accurately Simplify Patient-centered Information about Breast Cancer Prevention and Screening
evidence.outcome: Reading ease and readability of original vs ChatGPT-simplified responses to breast cancer questions
evidence.effect: Mean reading ease improved from 46 to 70 (P<.001); readability from grade 13 to 8.9 (P<.001); all 25 simplified responses met reading ease criteria, but only 2 of 25 (8%) met sixth-grade readability.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT improved mean reading ease (original responses, 46 vs simplified responses, 70; P < .001) and readability (original, grade 13 vs simplified, grade 8.9; P < .001) and decreased word count (original, 193 vs simplified, 173; P < .001).

evidence.title: Is ChatGPT a trusted source of information for total hip and knee arthroplasty patients?
evidence.outcome: simplified prompt readability and quality
evidence.effect: FKGL 11.14 vs 12.15 (p = 0.029); comprehensiveness 3.68 vs 3.91 (p = 0.027); accuracy/acceptability not significantly different.
evidence.quote: Between the original responses and the easier responses, there was no significant change in accuracy or acceptability, but there was a significant reduction in comprehensiveness and reading level.

evidence.title: ChatGPT vs. web search for patient questions: what does ChatGPT do better?
evidence.venue: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
evidence.outcome: readability after additional prompting
evidence.effect: Additional prompting improved readability: FRE 55.6 ± 13.6, p < 0.01.
evidence.quote: Additional prompting improved ChatGPT response readability (FRE 55.6 ± 13.6, p < 0.01).

evidence.title: Bridging the literacy gap for surgical consents: an AI-human expert collaborative approach
evidence.outcome: Readability of consent forms before vs after GPT-4 plain-language simplification
evidence.effect: Reading level fell from 13.9 to 8.9 (P = 0.004); Reading Ease rose from 35.3 to 63.8 (P < 0.001); passive voice fell from 38.4% to 20.0%; word rarity fell.
evidence.quote: After simplification, there was a significant decrease in the Reading Level (before = 13.9 vs. after = 8.9, P = 0.004) and improvement in Reading Ease (before = 35.3 vs. after = 63.8 P < 0.001) from the reading level of a college freshman to that of an 8th grade student.
evidence.sample_unit: consent forms from academic medical centers

evidence.title: From technical to understandable: Artificial Intelligence Large Language Models improve the readability of knee radiology reports
evidence.venue: Knee surgery, sports traumatology, arthroscopy : official journal of the ESSKA
evidence.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading level and reading ease of original vs AI-LLM patient-language reports
evidence.effect: Mean FKRL fell from 12.7 to 7.2 (X-ray), 13.4 to 7.5 (CT), 13.5 to 7.5 (MRI); FRE rose from 39.5 to 76.8, 27.3 to 73.1, 26.8 to 73.4; all statistically significant.
evidence.quote: Statistically significant improvements in mean FKRL scores in the AI-LLM generated X-ray report (12.7 ± 1.0-7.2 ± 0.6), CT report (13.4 ± 1.0-7.5 ± 0.5) and MRI report (13.5 ± 0.9-7.5 ± 0.6) were observed.

evidence.title: Using Large Language Models to Generate Educational Materials on Childhood Glaucoma
evidence.outcome: Readability (SMOG, FKGL) of LLM patient education materials with explicit 6th-grade prompt versus general understandability prompt
evidence.effect: Prompt B (6th-grade SMOG) responses were more readable than Prompt A for all 3 LLMs (P ≤ .001); ChatGPT-4 most readable.
evidence.quote: Prompt B responses were more readable than Prompt A responses for all 3 LLM (P ≤ .001).
evidence.sample_unit: LLM-generated patient education materials (3 LLMs, 3 prompts; 20 existing online resources rewritten)

evidence.title: Accuracy, readability, and understandability of large language models for prostate cancer information to the public
evidence.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT responses before vs after prompting for a 6th-grade level summary
evidence.effect: Flesch Grade Level 12.8(1.2) v. 7.4(1.7), p<0.0001; Flesch Reading Ease 36.5 v. 70.2; all six readability metrics improved. MTurk understanding of summaries 63.0-87.4%.
evidence.quote: Implementing a prompt that instructed GPT/LLM to produce a simplified answer to the prostate cancer question successfully improved the objective readability metrics.
evidence.sample_unit: prostate cancer questions (ChatGPT responses rated by 53 urologists/residents and 514 MTurk workers)

evidence.title: Improving Readability and Automating Content Analysis of Plastic Surgery Webpages With ChatGPT
evidence.outcome: Readability scores of original vs ChatGPT-revised webpage text
evidence.effect: Significant improvements in six readability metric scores using specific-instruction prompt with ChatGPT 3.5 (all P ≤ 0.05); no further improvement with ChatGPT 4.0.
evidence.quote: Significant improvements were achieved from baseline in six readability metric scores using a specific-instruction prompt with ChatGPT 3.5 (all P ≤ 0.05).

evidence.title: The Use of Artificial Intelligence to Improve Readability of Otolaryngology Patient Education Materials
evidence.venue: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery
evidence.outcome: Plain-language readability of patient education materials after AI conversion, with accuracy and content retention
evidence.effect: Average FKGL 11.03 to 5.80; converted materials retained enough detail with no factual errors.
evidence.quote: Converted materials provided enough detail for patient education with no factual errors.

evidence.title: Use of Artificial Intelligence Chatbots in Interpretation of Pathology Reports
evidence.outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid grade level) of original vs chatbot-simplified pathology reports
evidence.effect: Grade level fell from 13.19 to 8.17 (chatbot 1) and 7.45 (chatbot 2); Flesch Reading Ease rose from 10.32 to 61.32 and 70.80 (all P<.001).
evidence.quote: For the 1134 reports included, the Flesch-Kincaid grade level decreased from a mean of 13.19 (95% CI, 12.98-13.41) to 8.17 (95% CI, 8.08-8.25; t = 45.29; P < .001) by chatbot 1 and 7.45 (95% CI, 7.35-7.54; t = 49.69; P < .001) by chatbot 2.

evidence.title: ChatGPT-4 Can Help Hand Surgeons Communicate Better With Patients
evidence.venue: Journal of hand surgery global online
evidence.outcome: Whether ChatGPT-4 rewriting produces plain-language patient education material
evidence.effect: Mean FRE rose from 61.6 to 76.9 (P<.001); grade-level scores fell across all six formulas; word count fell from 728.3 to 303.6.
evidence.quote: The mean (± SD) FRE in the pre- and post-ChatGPT-4–edited text samples was 61.6 (±7.5) and 76.9 (± 8.2), respectively ( P < .001).

evidence.title: Patient-centered radiology reports with generative artificial intelligence: adding value to radiology reporting
evidence.outcome: Non-physician rater comprehension of original vs AI patient-friendly radiology reports (5-point Likert)
evidence.effect: Mean comprehension rose from 2.71 ± 0.73 for original reports to 4.69 ± 0.48 for patient-friendly reports (p < 0.001).
evidence.quote: The average comprehension score for the original report was 2.71 ± 0.73, while the score for the patient-friendly reports significantly increased to 4.69 ± 0.48 (p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Enhancing Health Literacy: Evaluating the Readability of Patient Handouts Revised by ChatGPT's Large Language Model
evidence.venue: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery
evidence.outcome: PEMAT understandability and actionability of native vs LLM-revised handouts
evidence.effect: Understandability 91% vs 74% (P<.05); actionability similar, 42% vs 34% (P=.15).
evidence.quote: PEMAT scores were significantly higher in the LLM-revised handouts for understandability (91 vs 74%; P < .05) with similar actionability (42 vs 34%; P = .15) when compared to the standard materials.

evidence.title: Decoding Radiology Reports: Artificial Intelligence-Large Language Models Can Improve the Readability of Hand and Wrist Orthopedic Radiology Reports
evidence.outcome: Readability (FRES, FKRL) of LLM-generated plain-language reports versus original radiology reports
evidence.effect: Statistically significant improvement in mean FRES and FKRL for radiograph, CT, and MRI reports; mean reading level of all AI-LLM-generated reports improved to below an eighth-grade level.
evidence.quote: For all AI-LLM-generated reports, the mean reading level improved to below an eighth-grade reading level.

evidence.title: Large language models: a new frontier in paediatric cataract patient education
evidence.outcome: Readability (SMOG, FKGL) of LLM patient education materials with explicit sixth-grade prompt versus generic prompt
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-3.5 and ChatGPT-4 prompt B responses were more readable than prompt A (p<0.001); ChatGPT-4 SMOG 5.59±0.5, FKGL 4.31±0.7; rewrote existing PEMs to SMOG 5.14±0.3.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-3.5 and ChatGPT-4 prompt B responses were more readable than prompt A responses (p<0.001).

evidence.title: Generating colloquial radiology reports with large language models
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
evidence.outcome: Readability of LLM-generated colloquial radiology reports versus original reports
evidence.effect: Translations were more readable than original reports by standard readability indices; 8th-grade level balanced accuracy and readability.
evidence.quote: Overall, translations were more readable than the original reports, as evaluated using standard readability indices.

evidence.title: Improving readability and comprehension levels of otolaryngology patient education materials using ChatGPT
evidence.outcome: Whether LLM simplification makes patient education materials more plain-language and readable
evidence.effect: Materials were written above recommended reading levels; ChatGPT translation significantly improved FRE and FK scores (p < 0.001), though ChatGPT self-scoring exaggerated the improvement relative to Word.
evidence.quote: Otolaryngology patient education materials were found to be written at higher reading levels than recommended.
evidence.sample_unit: patient education topics (37 ALA and 72 AAO-HNS)

evidence.title: Prompt engineering with ChatGPT3.5 and GPT4 to improve patient education on retinal diseases
evidence.venue: Canadian journal of ophthalmology. Journal canadien d'ophtalmologie
evidence.outcome: Readability, accuracy and comprehensiveness of LLM patient education responses under prompt engineering
evidence.effect: Prompt engineering improved readability (grade 13.45 to 10.3) but prompt B reduced accuracy and comprehensiveness (median 4.0 vs 5.0, p < 0.001).
evidence.quote: Prompt engineering can significantly improve readability of LLM-generated responses, although at the cost of reducing accuracy and comprehensiveness.
evidence.sample_unit: patient questions (each run under 3 prompt conditions in 2 LLMs)

evidence.title: Expanding Accessibility in Cleft Care: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Improving Literacy of Alveolar Bone Grafting Information
evidence.venue: The Cleft palate-craniofacial journal : official publication of the American Cleft Palate-Craniofacial Association
evidence.outcome: Readability of patient education materials before and after ChatGPT rewriting
evidence.effect: ChatGPT rewriting improved Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level to 6.1 ± 1.3 (p < 0.0001) from 8.0 ± 2.3.
evidence.quote: PEM rewriting with ChatGPT improved Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level to 6.1 ± 1.3 (p < 0.0001).

evidence.title: Can generative AI improve the readability of patient education materials at a radiology practice?
evidence.outcome: readability after AI simplification
evidence.effect: ChatGPT ARL 7.32 ± 0.76; Gemini ARL 6.55 ± 0.51.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT ARL was 7.32 ± 0.76 (6/7 significant) and Gemini ARL was 6.55 ± 0.51 (7/7 significant).

evidence.title: Bridging Gaps in Health Literacy for Cleft Lip and Palate: The Role of Artificial Intelligence and Interactive Educational Materials
evidence.venue: The Cleft palate-craniofacial journal : official publication of the American Cleft Palate-Craniofacial Association
evidence.outcome: Readability and clarity of patient education materials before and after ChatGPT-4 simplification
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4 modification significantly improved readability from median 9th-grade to median 6th-grade level with enhanced clarity.
evidence.quote: Modifications using ChatGPT-4 significantly improved readability, achieving a median 6th-grade level and enhanced clarity.

evidence.title: ChatGPT for improving postoperative instructions in multiple fields of plastic surgery
evidence.venue: Journal of plastic, reconstructive & aesthetic surgery : JPRAS
evidence.outcome: understandability and actionability
evidence.effect: Understandability scores increased as reading levels decreased, whereas actionability decreased for fourth-grade rewrites.
evidence.quote: Understandability scores increased as reading levels decreased, whereas actionability scores decreased for fourth-grade rewrites.

evidence.title: Advancing Patient Education in Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension: The Promise of Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: Readability, quality and accuracy of PEMs rewritten to plain language by LLMs
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4 rewrote published PEMs to below 6th-grade level (SMOG 5.6 ± 0.6, FKGL 5.7 ± 0.8, p<0.001) without decrease in quality (DISCERN ≥4) or accuracy (Likert misinformation = 1).
evidence.quote: Original published PEMs were rewritten to below a 6th-grade reading level with Prompt C, without a decrease in quality, understandability, or accuracy only by ChatGPT-4 (SMOG: 5.6 ± 0.6, FKGL: 5.7 ± 0.8, p < 0.001, DISCERN ≥4, Likert misinformation = 1).
evidence.sample_unit: LLM-generated and rewritten patient education materials

evidence.title: Evaluation of the Appropriateness and Readability of ChatGPT-4 Responses to Patient Queries on Uveitis
evidence.outcome: Readability of simplified patient education responses
evidence.effect: Simplified ChatGPT-4 FKGL was 6.08–7.03 across sources versus standard 10.25–11.26 and existing websites 7.05–9.67.
evidence.quote: The simplified ChatGPT-4 responses consistently exhibited a pattern where the required reading comprehension level, as determined by the FKGL metric, corresponded to sixth to seventh grade ( Table 5 ).

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence improves urologic oncology patient education and counseling
evidence.outcome: readability after education-level adjustment
evidence.effect: Readability improved to 7.50 for ChatGPT-a and 3.53 for Epic Easy to Read; only ChatGPT-a retained high quality.
evidence.quote: When adjusted for user education level (ChatGPT-a and Epic Easy to Read), readability improved (7.50 and 3.53), but only ChatGPT-a retained high quality.
evidence.sample_unit: patient education materials (prostate, bladder, kidney cancer)

evidence.title: Utilizing Artificial Intelligence to Increase the Readability of Patient Education Materials in Pediatric Otolaryngology
evidence.outcome: Readability grade level of patient education materials before and after ChatGPT simplification to fifth-grade level
evidence.effect: AAO-HNS materials fell from 10.71 ± 0.71 to 7.9 ± 1.18 (P<.01); combined materials fell from 9.32 ± 1.82 to 7.68 ± 1.12 (P=.0598); not all materials reached recommended level.
evidence.quote: However, it did not possess the capability to reduce all materials to be below the recommended reading level.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence as a modality to enhance the readability of neurosurgical literature for patients
evidence.outcome: Readability of AI-generated layperson summaries versus original abstracts (grade-level indices)
evidence.effect: Flesch-Kincaid grade fell from 12.55 (original) to 7.80 (GPT3.5) and 7.70 (GPT4), p<0.0001; reading ease rose from 33.29 to 68.45 and 69.55.
evidence.quote: Flesch-Kincaid reading grade (12.55, 7.80, 7.70, p < 0.0001)

evidence.title: Enhancing Access to Orthopedic Education: Exploring the Potential of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Improving Health Literacy on Rotator Cuff Injuries
evidence.outcome: Readability and length of patient education materials after plain-language rewriting by generative AI
evidence.effect: Rewritten PEMs averaged 5.67 grade level versus 10.02 originally; word count fell from 755.0 to 312.2 (mean reduction 442.68, p < 0.001).
evidence.quote: Following the application of ChatGPT's rewriting tool, all 25 PEMs were revised to meet readability standards below the eighth-grade level.

evidence.title: Leveraging large language models to improve patient education on dry eye disease
evidence.outcome: Readability of LLM-rewritten patient education materials at 6th-grade target
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4 and Gemini Advanced rewrote existing PEMs from baseline FKGL 8.0 ± 2.4, SMOG 7.9 ± 1.7 to targeted 6th-grade level; rewrites had little to no misinformation (median Likert 1).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4 and Gemini Advanced rewrote existing PEMs (Prompt C) from a baseline readability level (FKGL: 8.0 ± 2.4, SMOG: 7.9 ± 1.7) to targeted 6th-grade reading level; rewrites contained little to no misinformation (median Likert misinformation=1 (range: 1-2)).

evidence.title: Large Language Models May Help Patients Understand Peer-Reviewed Scientific Articles About Ophthalmology: Development and Usability Study
evidence.outcome: Readability grade level of papers before and after ChatGPT plain-language simplification; ophthalmologist appropriateness
evidence.effect: Readability fell from 15th to 7th grade (P<.001), and expert ophthalmologists judged the simplified responses appropriate. The output was still above the 6th-grade target.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT significantly lowered the readability and length of the selected papers from 15th to 7th grade (P<.001) while generating responses that were deemed appropriate by expert ophthalmologists.

evidence.title: The literacy barrier in clinical trial consents: a retrospective analysis
evidence.outcome: Reading level and word count of consent sections before and after GPT-4 simplification with expert review
evidence.effect: FK grade fell across all sections (e.g., Alternatives 10.33 to 4.48; Confidentiality 14.5 to 5.70; P<0.001); expert review of 20 forms found them medically and legally equally sufficient.
evidence.quote: After simplification, the Flesh-Kincaid Grade Level significantly decreased across all sections, with Alternatives reducing to a Flesh-Kincaid Grade of 4.48 (P < 0.001) and the Confidentiality clause to a Flesh-Kincaid Grade of 5.70 (P < 0.001).

evidence.title: Evaluation of Multilingual Simplifications of IR Procedural Reports Using GPT-4
evidence.venue: Journal of vascular and interventional radiology : JVIR
evidence.outcome: Readability and layperson comprehension of GPT-4 plain-language summaries versus original IR reports
evidence.effect: FKRL improved from 10.7 to 7.0 and FRES from 41.9 to 73.0; layperson comprehension rose significantly from 2.5 to 4.3 out of 5.
evidence.quote: Layperson comprehension scores improved significantly from 2.5 to 4.3 out of 5 after summarization.

evidence.title: Enhancing patient education on the role of tibial osteotomy in the management of knee osteoarthritis using a customized ChatGPT: a readability and quality assessment
evidence.outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient education responses, plain-language customization vs native model
evidence.effect: Knee Guide FKGL 8.2 (range 5–10.7) vs ChatGPT-4 13.99 (range 11–16); FRES 60 vs 32; significant difference (p ≤ 0.001).
evidence.quote: Answers produced by “The Knee Guide” had a significantly lower RGL than those produced by ChatGPT 4 ( p ≤ 0.001).

evidence.title: Assessing ChatGPT Responses to Frequently Asked Patient Questions in Reconstructive Urology
evidence.outcome: understandability and actionability
evidence.effect: Prompt engineering improved understandability 89.6% to 96.2% and actionability 38.3% to 93.5% (both P < .001).
evidence.quote: Using prompt engineering in the incontinence domain, scores for DISCERN (3.57-4.75, P = .007), PEMAT-P understandability (89.6% to 96.2%, P < .001), actionability (38.3% to 93.5%, P < .001), and reading level (grade 12.4-5.4, P < .01) all improved significantly while misinformation and word count did not change significantly.

evidence.title: Readability of Hospital Online Patient Education Materials Across Otolaryngology Specialties
evidence.outcome: Readability, accuracy, content and tone of ChatGPT-4o generated patient education materials versus hospital and organization materials
evidence.effect: ChatGPT OPEMs averaged 6.8 grade level, more readable than hospital and organization OPEMs (p ≤ 0.016) with accuracy 4.8-4.9/5; re-prompting for below sixth grade lowered content scores.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT‐4o generated OPEMs were consistently more readable than both hospital and institutional OPEMs across all specialties ( p ≤ 0.016), except for ENTUK in facial plastics (6.6 vs. 7.2, p = 0.219).
evidence.sample_unit: hospitals (online patient education materials for seven otolaryngology procedures)

evidence.title: Potential role of ChatGPT in simplifying and improving informed consent forms for vaccination: a pilot study conducted in Italy
evidence.outcome: Readability (Gulpease) and professional ratings of consent forms: human standard vs ChatGPT-rewritten vs fully ChatGPT-generated
evidence.effect: Gulpease: A 36, B 66, C 82 (C most readable). Professionals rated A and C highest; B lowest (overall median 3.0 A and C vs 2.0 B); A vs C not significantly different.
evidence.quote: Using the Gulpease Index, the scores obtained for each consent form were: 36 for consent form A, namely incomprehensible for elementary level, very difficult for middle and high school levels.

evidence.title: Evaluating the Performance of Artificial Intelligence for Improving Readability of Online English- and Spanish-Language Orthopaedic Patient Educational Material: Challenges in Bridging the Digital Divide
evidence.venue: The Journal of bone and joint surgery. American volume
evidence.outcome: Readability, word count, complex words and long sentences of patient education materials after AI plain-language rewrite
evidence.effect: Grade level reduced 2.0 ± 1.8 (English) and 1.5 ± 1.2 (Spanish); word count, complex words, and long sentences significantly reduced while maintaining high accuracy and similarity.
evidence.quote: Word count, use of complex words, and long sentences were also reduced significantly in both languages while still maintaining high accuracy and similarity compared with original content.
evidence.sample_unit: online patient educational materials (57 English, 56 Spanish)

evidence.title: Using ChatGPT to Improve the Presentation of Plain Language Summaries of Cochrane Systematic Reviews About Oncology Interventions: Cross-Sectional Study
evidence.outcome: readability of patient summaries
evidence.effect: Prompt 1 median SMOG 8.2 (95% CI 8-8.4) vs original 13.1 (95% CI 12.9-13.4).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-generated PLSs using the first prompt (SMOG index 6) were the shortest and easiest to read, with a median SMOG score of 8.2 (95% CI 8-8.4), compared with the original PLSs (median SMOG score 13.1, 95% CI 12.9-13.4).
evidence.sample_unit: Cochrane oncology plain language summaries (each generated with 3 prompts)

evidence.title: Improving readability of shoulder and elbow surgery online patient education material with Chat GPT (Chat Generative Pretrained Transformer) 4
evidence.venue: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery
evidence.outcome: Readability (SMOG) of patient education material before vs after ChatGPT-4 plain-language simplification
evidence.effect: SMOG dropped from 10.1 to 8.3 and ChatGPT-assessed level from 10.3 to 7.7 after simplification (P < .001), near recommended levels.
evidence.quote: Following simplification, both the SMOG readability score and ChatGPT significantly dropped to 8.3 and 7.7, respectively, aligning closer to recommended readability levels (P < .001).

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT for converting clinic letters into patient-friendly language: a quantitative study
evidence.outcome: Patient representatives' understanding, satisfaction, need for help, and clinical information loss for AI plain-language letters versus originals
evidence.effect: No loss of clinical information; significant increase in understanding and satisfaction, and decreased need to obtain medical help to translate letter contents, versus clinician-written originals.
evidence.quote: Translation of letters by ChatGPT-4 Classic resulted in no loss of clinical information, but did result in significant increase in understanding, satisfaction, and decrease in the need to obtain medical help to translate the letter contents by patient representatives compared with clinician-written originals.

evidence.title: Online patient information on labour epidural analgesia provided by UK National Health Services hospitals: assessment of readability and improvement of readability standards using ChatGPT
evidence.outcome: Readability of patient education texts after ChatGPT rewriting to sixth-grade level
evidence.effect: After AI-modification, 24.6% and 27.5% met targets; mean grade fell from 8.4 to 7.7 (P<0.001) but still missed the target level.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT can be used to enhance readability but also fails to meet recommended health literacy standards.

evidence.title: [Making prostate cancer research accessible: chatGPT-4 as a tool to enhance lay communication]
evidence.outcome: readability of lay summaries
evidence.effect: Advanced prompt improved readability vs basic prompt and original LS; both p<0.001.
evidence.quote: The advanced prompt led to significantly improved readability compared to the basic prompt (p < 0.001) and the original LS (p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Enhancing Physician-Patient Communication in Oncology Using GPT-4 Through Simplified Radiology Reports: Multicenter Quantitative Study
evidence.outcome: Lay comprehension, reading time, and consultation time for original vs GPT-4 simplified radiology reports
evidence.effect: Comprehension scores rose from 5.51 to 7.83 (P<.001); consultation time fell from 1116.11 to 745.30 seconds (P<.001); reading rate rose from 72.15 to 104.70 words per minute.
evidence.quote: Physician-patient communication time significantly decreased, from 1116.11 seconds to 745.30 seconds (P<.001), and patient comprehension scores improved from 5.51 to 7.83 (P<.001).

evidence.title: Large Language Models: Pioneering New Educational Frontiers in Childhood Myopia
evidence.outcome: Readability of existing online patient education materials after LLM plain-language rewriting
evidence.effect: Original online PEMs FKGL 9.7 and SMOG 10.3; after rewriting ChatGPT-4o FKGL 5.8, ChatGPT-3.5 7.7, Gemini 7.5 (p<0.001).
evidence.quote: Using prompt C, the three LLMs significantly improved the readability of existing online educational resources, as evidenced by a marked enhancement in average readability scores ( p ≤ 0.001) (Fig. 2 ).

evidence.title: PRECISE framework: Enhanced radiology reporting with GPT for improved readability, reliability, and patient-centered care
evidence.outcome: Understandability of plain-language AI-generated radiology summaries rated by non-medical volunteers and reliability by clinicians
evidence.effect: Non-medical volunteers rated 97% of PRECISE summaries fully understandable; clinicians found 95% reliable.
evidence.quote: Clinical volunteer assessments found 95 % of the summaries reliable, and non-medical volunteers rated 97 % of the PRECISE-generated summaries as fully understandable.

evidence.title: The role of large language models in improving the readability of orthopaedic spine patient educational material
evidence.venue: Journal of orthopaedic surgery and research
evidence.outcome: Readability and accuracy of LLM-simplified patient education text versus original
evidence.effect: Reading Ease improved significantly across steps (p<0.0001), greatest at Step 1 (mean gains 14-18 points); word count fell by about 1000 words; grade level rose at Step 1 then declined; accuracy stable, no hallucinations observed.
evidence.quote: Reading Ease improved significantly across steps ( p < 0.0001), with the greatest improvement between the original articles and Step 1, and smaller but still significant gains from Step 1 to Step 2 (Table 3 , Fig. 2 B).

evidence.title: Enhancing the Readability of Online Patient Education Materials Using Large Language Models: Cross-Sectional Study
evidence.outcome: Readability of LLM-simplified patient education materials versus originals (average grade level)
evidence.effect: Average grade level improved from 10.1 to 7.6 (ChatGPT), 6.6 (Gemini), and 5.6 (Claude), all P<.001; understandability (PEMAT-U) largely preserved.
evidence.quote: Compared with the original website, ChatGPT improved the readability to 7.6 from 10.1 ( P <.001); Gemini, to 6.6 ( P <.001); and Claude, to 5.6 ( P <.001).

evidence.title: Improving Patient Communication by Simplifying AI-Generated Dental Radiology Reports With ChatGPT: Comparative Study
evidence.outcome: Readability and patient-rated comprehension of original vs ChatGPT-simplified radiology reports
evidence.effect: FRE 51.1 (original) vs 55.0 and 56.4 (simplified), P<.001; ability to understand findings without help: mean 1.5 (SD 0.7) text 3 vs 3.1 (SD 1.4) text 1.
evidence.quote: Both simplified report versions (texts 2 and 3) received significantly better ratings across all evaluated aspects, highlighting a preference for more accessible medical documents in the future.

evidence.title: Online platform vs. doctors: a comparative exploration of congenital cataract patient education from virtual to reality
evidence.outcome: Whether plain-language rewriting of AI patient education responses improves readability without loss of quality
evidence.effect: After simplification, difficult words halved; readability, helpfulness and safety significantly improved in RE-CD (p<0.05); correctness decreased in RE-CG.
evidence.quote: Moreover, in the RE-CD group, Readability, Helpfulness, and Safety indicated significant improvement (Mann–Whitney U Test, p < 0.05) ( Figures 5B , C ).

evidence.title: Large Language Model-Assisted Surgical Consent Forms in Non-English Language: Content Analysis and Readability Evaluation
evidence.outcome: Readability of LLM-simplified Korean consent forms (KReaD and Natmal scores)
evidence.effect: KReaD fell from 1777 (SD 28.47) to 1335.6 (SD 59.95), P<.001; Natmal from 1452.3 (SD 88.67) to 1245.3 (SD 96.96), P=.007. Sentence length and difficult word ratio decreased.
evidence.quote: Artificial intelligence-assisted editing significantly improved readability, reducing the KReaD score from 1777 (SD 28.47) to 1335.6 (SD 59.95) (P<.001) and the Natmal score from 1452.3 (SD 88.67) to 1245.3 (SD 96.96) (P=.007).
evidence.sample_unit: surgical consent forms (liver resection) from 7 institutions, rated by 7 specialists

evidence.title: Improving the Readability of Institutional Heart Failure-Related Patient Education Materials Using GPT-4: Observational Study
evidence.outcome: Readability and accuracy of GPT-4 plain-language rewrites of patient education materials
evidence.effect: Median FKGL fell from 10.3 to 7.3 (P<.001); PEMs below sixth-grade level rose from 9.1% to 23.1%; none graded less accurate or less comprehensive.
evidence.quote: No revised GPT-4 PEMs were graded as less accurate or less comprehensive compared to institutional PEMs.

evidence.title: The Use of ChatGPT-4.0 to Simplify Breast Pathology Reports: A Study on Readability and Accuracy
evidence.outcome: Readability of AI-simplified pathology reports for patients
evidence.effect: ChatGPT simplified reports to recommended reading level with grade-level specification while mostly maintaining accuracy (overall accuracy 3.59/4).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT simplified breast pathology reports to the reading level recommended for patient-facing materials when given a grade-level specification while mostly maintaining accuracy.

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence-simplified information to advance reproductive genetic literacy and health equity
evidence.outcome: Readability of LLM-simplified patient education materials, plus expert-rated accuracy and completeness
evidence.effect: All four LLMs significantly improved readability (P<0.001) to about 6th-7th grade level; GPT-4 had highest expert ratings for accuracy (4.1±0.9), completeness (4.2±0.8), and relevance of omissions (4.0±0.9).
evidence.quote: All four LLMs significantly improved the readability of the PEMs (P-values <0.001), reducing text complexity to an average 6th-7th grade reading level.

evidence.title: Using large language models to generate child-friendly education materials on myopia
evidence.outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient education with plain-language child-targeted prompt vs adult prompt
evidence.effect: Prompt B responses had significantly higher readability (FKGL, FRE, syllables/word) for all LLMs (p ≤ 0.001); dominant reading level moved from college/10th–12th grade to 6th–7th grade.
evidence.quote: Specifically, responses to prompt B exhibit higher readability scores in terms of FKGL, FRE score, average syllables per word, and reading level.
evidence.sample_unit: questions (each answered by 4 LLMs under 2 prompts; 280 responses per prompt)

evidence.title: Readability of custom chatbot vs. GPT-4 responses to otolaryngology-related patient questions
evidence.outcome: Readability (FKGL, FRE) of custom plain-language GPT vs GPT-4 responses
evidence.effect: Custom GPT reduced FKGL by an average of 4.2 grade levels (95% CI 3.2, 5.1; p<0.001) and increased FRE by 17.3 points (95% CI 12.5, 21.7; p<0.001).
evidence.quote: The custom GPT reduced FKGL by an average of 4.2 grade levels (95 % confidence interval [CI]: 3.2, 5.1; p < 0.001) and increased FRE by an average of 17.3 points (95 % CI: 12.5, 21.7; p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Assessing Readability, Understandability, and Actionability of ACPA Educational Resources and Utility of LLMs to Improve Accessibility for Caregivers
evidence.venue: The Cleft palate-craniofacial journal : official publication of the American Cleft Palate-Craniofacial Association
evidence.outcome: Reading level, understandability, actionability of caregiver materials after LLM plain-language modification
evidence.effect: LLM modification reduced reading level to 8.0 ± 1.2 (P = .0002); understandability 80.5% (P = .5371) and actionability 40.8% (P = .6709) not significantly changed.
evidence.quote: Modification by LLMs decreased average reading level to 8.0 ± 1.2 (P = .0002) with a PEMAT understandability of 80.5 ± 7.9% (P = .5371) and actionability of 40.8 ± 18.2% (P = .6709).

evidence.title: ChatGPT-4o as a digital health tool for diabetes technology education: insights on reliability, quality, and readability
evidence.outcome: Readability (FKGL, FRE) of ChatGPT-4o responses before and after 'explain in simpler terms' prompt
evidence.effect: Simplification prompt improved readability significantly (mean FKGL: 4.9; FRE: 79.0) without altering content; baseline English responses required college-level literacy (FKGL 10.5, FRE 37.8).
evidence.quote: Prompting simplification improved readability significantly (mean FKGL: 4.9; FRE: 79.0), without altering content.

evidence.title: Application of artificial intelligence chatbots in interpreting magnetic resonance imaging reports: a comparative study
evidence.outcome: Readability of chatbot-translated MRI reports (Flesch-Kincaid Reading Ease, Gunning Fog)
evidence.effect: Both chatbots significantly improved readability; Chatbot 2 achieved higher Flesch-Kincaid Reading Ease scores (median 58.70 vs. 46.00, p < 0.001) and lower text complexity.
evidence.quote: Both chatbots significantly improved readability, with Chatbot 2 achieving higher Flesch-Kincaid Reading Ease scores (median: 58.70 vs. 46.00, p < 0.001) and lower text complexity.

evidence.title: Evaluating the Quality and Understandability of Radiology Report Summaries Generated by ChatGPT: Survey Study
evidence.outcome: Patient confidence, satisfaction with jargon and time to understand: original report vs ChatGPT plain-language summary
evidence.effect: Confidence in understanding 98% (116/118) with summary vs 26% (31/118) with report; jargon satisfaction 91% vs 8%; time to understand 97% vs 23%.
evidence.quote: After reading the summary, patient confidence in understanding (98%, 116/118 vs 26%, 31/118) and satisfaction regarding the level of jargon/terminology (91%, 107/118 vs 8%, 9/118) and time taken to understand the content (97%, 115/118 vs 23%, 27/118) substantially improved.
evidence.sample_unit: radiology reports (evaluated by 4 neuroradiologists and 4 patient volunteers)

evidence.title: Assessing the ability of large language models to simplify lumbar spine imaging reports into patient-facing text: a pilot study of GPT-4
evidence.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading level of patient-facing translations
evidence.effect: Average grade level fell from 11.47 (SD 1.44) in original reports to 8.50 (SD 1.27) with base prompt, p < 0.001.
evidence.quote: With the base prompt, the average word count was not significantly changed (399.64 SD 72.70, p = 0.510) though the average reading level was significantly decreased to between 8 and 9th grade (8.50 SD 1.27, p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Enhancing Readability of Lay Abstracts and Summaries for Urologic Oncology Literature Using Generative Artificial Intelligence: BRIDGE-AI 6 Randomized Controlled Trial
evidence.outcome: Patient/caregiver comprehension and perception of AI plain-language summaries vs original abstracts
evidence.effect: LAS recipients scored significantly better in comprehension and most perception questions (P<.001); readability 68.9 vs 25.3 (P<.001); LAS was the only consistently significant predictor.
evidence.quote: GAI-generated LAS recipients scored significantly better in comprehension and most perception-based questions (P < .001) with LAS being the only consistently significant predictor (P < .001).
evidence.sample_unit: patients and caregivers (randomized); 40 abstracts, 600 generated sections

evidence.title: AI-Generated Patient-Friendly MRI Fistula Summaries: A Pilot Randomised Study
evidence.outcome: Patient-rated readability and comprehensibility of AI plain-language MRI summaries versus original reports; Flesch-Kincaid score
evidence.effect: Patients rated AI summaries higher for readability (median 5 vs 2, p=0.011) and comprehensibility (5 vs 2, p=0.007); Flesch-Kincaid 54.6 vs 32.2 (p=0.005); no clinically significant inaccuracies.
evidence.quote: Patients rated AI summaries significantly higher in readability (median 5 vs. 2, p = 0.011), comprehensibility (5 vs. 2, p = 0.007), utility (5 vs. 3, p = 0.014), and overall quality (4.5 vs. 4, p = 0.013), with fewer follow-up questions (3 vs. 4, p = 0.018).

evidence.title: Utilizing artificial intelligence to increase the readability of patient education materials in pediatric neurosurgery
evidence.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid grade level of patient education materials before and after ChatGPT plain-language rewriting
evidence.effect: ChatGPT reduced mean reading level from 10.60 (SD 0.57) to 6.18 (SD 0.28; p < 0.05), reaching the 6th-grade target across all conditions.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT effectively reduced the mean reading level from 10.60 (SD 0.57) to 6.18 (SD 0.28; p < 0.05), achieving the target 6th-grade level across all conditions.

evidence.title: Refining patient education on autologous chondrocyte implantation for chondral lesions of the knee: A fine-tuned ChatGPT-4o model improves readability and quality
evidence.outcome: Readability and quality of AI patient education responses, fine-tuned vs native model
evidence.effect: Fine-tuned ACI Guide FKGL 9.25 vs 13.45 native; FRES 49.59 vs 35.68 (p<0.001); DISCERN 43.18 vs 35.29 (p<0.001).
evidence.quote: The ACI Guide achieved a mean DISCERN score of 43.18 ± 3.92 (range: 34–53), reflecting moderate‐quality responses, while the native ChatGPT‐4o scored 35.29 ± 5.0 (range: 23–45; p < 0.001), indicating poor‐quality responses.

evidence.title: Readability versus accuracy in LLM-transformed radiology reports: stakeholder preferences across reading grade levels
evidence.outcome: readability and accuracy of generated reports
evidence.effect: Across reading grades 7-17, lower grades improved readability but increased errors; higher grades improved accuracy but reduced readability.
evidence.quote: Lower reading grades improved readability but increased errors, while higher grades improved accuracy but reduced readability.

evidence.title: Online patient information on temporomandibular disorders provided by UK NHS hospitals: assessment and improvement of readability standards using AI-chatbots
evidence.venue: The British journal of oral & maxillofacial surgery
evidence.outcome: Readability of AI-revised patient materials versus original, at sixth-grade target
evidence.effect: After Gemini revision, 96.8% met target per FKGL, 54.8% per GFI, 29.0% per CLI; mean FRES improved to 82.59 (5.73), p<0.001.
evidence.quote: AI chatbots, particularly Gemini, can significantly enhance the readability of these materials, enabling them to meet health literacy standards according to certain readability tools.
evidence.sample_unit: hospital Trust TMD patient information materials

evidence.title: Patient Perceptions on Operative Reports Written by Surgeons versus Versions Simplified by Artificial Intelligence
evidence.outcome: Patient preference and comprehension of AI-simplified versus original operative reports
evidence.effect: 55.4% preferred GPT-simplified reports; clearer (1.53 vs 1.98, P<0.001), more accessible terminology (1.50 vs 2.31, P<0.001), more understandable (86.40 vs 73.70, P<0.001).
evidence.quote: The primary outcome showed that 55.4% (95% CI: 48.6%-61.2%) of participants preferred the GPT-simplified reports for being significantly clearer (mean = 1.53 ± 0.83 vs. 1.98 ± 1.92, P < 0.001), terminology being more accessible (mean = 1.50 ± 0.70 vs. 2.31 ± 0.89, P < 0.001), and overall, more understandable (mean = 86.40 ± 18.07 vs. 73.70 ± 20.82, P < 0.001).

evidence.title: Evaluation of prostate cancer pathology reports generated by ChatGPT to enhance patient comprehension
evidence.outcome: Readability (Flesch Reading Ease) of AI-generated versus original pathology reports; patient and urologist ratings
evidence.effect: AI biopsy and surgical reports had higher Flesch Reading Ease Scores (49 ± 5; 50 ± 3) than originals (31 ± 15, p < 0.001; 41 ± 17, p = 0.02). 88% of patients found AI biopsy reports helpful for understanding diagnosis.
evidence.quote: The AI-generated biopsy and surgical pathology reports had higher mean Flesch Reading Ease Scores (49 ± 5; 50 ± 3) compared to the original reports (31 ± 15, p < 0.001; 41 ± 17, p = 0.02, respectively).

evidence.title: Assessing the accuracy and readability of ChatGPT 4.0's original and simplified responses to common patient questions regarding periacetabular osteotomy
evidence.outcome: Readability and accuracy of AI patient education responses after simplification prompts
evidence.effect: Simplify prompt lowered FK grade from 11.09 to 8.16; sixth-grade prompt gave 7.09. Accuracy remained high (no unsatisfactory responses) across prompt types.
evidence.quote: For simplified responses, the average Flesch‐Kincaid Grade Level for all responses was 8.16 ± 1.46 which correlates approximately to the reading level of an eighth grader.

evidence.title: GPT-4 as a source of patient information for cervical disc arthroplasty: a comparative analysis against Google web search
evidence.outcome: Readability of GPT-4 output after prompting to rewrite for low literacy versus initial output
evidence.effect: After the low-literacy rewrite prompt, FK grade fell from 13.06 to 6.58 and Reading Ease rose from 36.87 to 76.20 (P<0.001), with similar word count (218.6 vs 222.8).
evidence.quote: However, when GPT-4 was prompted to make its responses more readable, the Flesch-Kincaid grade level improved to 6.58, the Flesch Reading Ease score to 76.20, and the word count slightly decreased to 218.60.

evidence.title: Enhancing Patient Education with AI: A Readability Analysis of AI-Generated Versus American Academy of Ophthalmology Online Patient Education Materials
evidence.outcome: Readability change after follow-up prompt to rewrite at 6th-grade level
evidence.effect: FRO prompting improved readability to 8.3 (ChatGPT), 11.2 (Copilot), 9.3 (Llama) (p<0.001), but still above 6th grade and not statistically easier than AAO (8.0).
evidence.quote: While initially prompted ChatGPT, Copilot, and Llama outputs were 10.8, 12.2, and 13.2, respectively, FRO prompting significantly improved readability to 8.3 for ChatGPT, 11.2 for Copilot, and 9.3 for Llama (p < 0.001).
evidence.sample_unit: diagnoses (topics) for which patient education materials were generated per LLM

evidence.title: Utility and Limitations of Large Language Models to Simplify Online Content on Generalized Pustular Psoriasis
evidence.outcome: plain-language patient education quality
evidence.effect: LLMs improved readability, but did not preserve original reliability and quality.
evidence.quote: While LLMs improved readability, they did not preserve the original content's reliability and quality.
evidence.sample_unit: online web texts on generalized pustular psoriasis

evidence.title: ChatGPT-4 in Psychiatric Discharge Summaries: Toward a More Comprehensible and Emotionally Sensitive Clinical Communication
evidence.venue: The International journal of social psychiatry
evidence.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT-4 rewritten discharge summaries (Fernández-Huerta, INFLESZ) versus originals
evidence.effect: Significant readability improvement across all diagnostic groups (p < .001), with mean values above recommended thresholds; five summaries remained below thresholds.
evidence.quote: Significant improvements in readability were observed across all diagnostic groups (p < .001), with mean values surpassing recommended thresholds for general comprehension.

evidence.title: Using ChatGPT-4 for Lay Summarization in Prostate Cancer Research to Advance Patient-Centered Communication: Large-Scale Generative AI Performance Evaluation
evidence.outcome: Readability (FKRE) of AI lay summaries with simple vs extended plain-language prompt vs original
evidence.effect: Median FKRE extended prompt 47 (IQR 42-56), simple prompt 36 (29-43), original 20 (9.5-29); P<.001. High-quality: 79.4% extended, 54.9% simple, 5.4% original.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4-generated lay summaries showed an improvement in readability compared to human-written versions, with the extended prompt achieving higher scores than the simple prompt (median FKRE: extended prompt 47, IQR 42-56; simple prompt 36, IQR 29-43; original 20, IQR 9.5-29; P<.001).
evidence.sample_unit: prostate cancer articles (lay summaries per prompt)

evidence.title: Enhancing patient and parent education in pediatric ophthalmology using artificial intelligence: a report by the AAPOS Public Information Committee
evidence.venue: Journal of AAPOS : the official publication of the American Association for Pediatric Ophthalmology and Strabismus
evidence.outcome: Readability and understandability of LLM-rewritten patient education materials
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4 rewrites reached 7th-grade level; Gemini Advanced met 6th-grade threshold with modestly reduced quality; understandability 90.9% and 91.3% (P<0.001); no misinformation.
evidence.quote: Both models enhanced understandability (ChatGPT-4, 90.9%; Gemini Advanced, 91.3%; [P < 0.001]), and their rewrites contained no misinformation (Likert = 1).

evidence.title: Evaluation of the artificial intelligence chatbots in frequently asked questions about retinitis pigmentosa: a comparative analysis between ChatGPT-4 and Gemini-2.0
evidence.venue: International journal of retina and vitreous
evidence.outcome: Readability grade level of chatbot answers, standard versus sixth-grade simplified prompt
evidence.effect: Standard ChatGPT-4 ARLC 12.01 and Gemini 11.25 grade level; simplified ARLC 6.73 and 6.72. Accuracy Likert stayed ~4.8-4.97 (p=0.090 between models).
evidence.quote: In particular, almost all readability indices suggest that standard AI chatbot responses require a higher level of education for comprehension, whereas simplified responses require a lower level of education.

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence Can Answer Postoperative Questions About Distal Radius Fractures-But Can Patients Understand the Answers?
evidence.venue: Journal of hand surgery global online
evidence.outcome: readability after simplified prompts
evidence.effect: After simplification, ChatGPT improved to seventh-grade and Copilot to eighth-grade; Gemini remained unchanged.
evidence.quote: After simplification, Gemini's reading level remained unchanged, whereas ChatGPT improved to that of a seventh-grade reading level and Copilot improved to that of an eighth-grade reading level.

evidence.title: ChatGPT-generated informed consent forms in interventional radiology: A randomized controlled evaluation of comprehension, attitudinal responses, and readability
evidence.outcome: Comprehension of AI-generated plain-language consent forms versus standard forms
evidence.effect: Comprehension 82.9% with ChatGPT forms vs 77.3% with standard forms (p = 0.04); forms had shorter sentences and lower linguistic complexity (Flesch 39.2; Ateşman 53.9).
evidence.quote: Participants who read ChatGPT-generated consent forms achieved higher comprehension scores than those who read standard forms (82.9 % vs. 77.3 %, p = 0.04).

evidence.title: Accuracy and Readability of Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer-4 Omni in Answering Ophthalmology Patient Questions
evidence.outcome: Sixth-grade prompt answer quality
evidence.effect: Accurate/complete increased from 220/285 (77.2%) to 242/285 (84.9%); unacceptable decreased from 16 (5.6%) to 5 (1.8%).
evidence.quote: When asked to respond at a sixth-grade reading level, 242 (85%) responses were graded as accurate and complete, 38 (13%) were incomplete, and 5 (2%) were graded as unacceptable.

evidence.title: Enhancing Patient Understanding of Perianal Fistula MRI Findings Using ChatGPT: A Randomized, Single Centre Study
evidence.outcome: Patient-rated readability, comprehension, usefulness, and Flesch-Kincaid score of AI plain-language summaries versus original MRI reports
evidence.effect: AI summaries scored significantly higher for readability, comprehension, and usefulness than original reports (all p<0.001), with equivalent trust; mean Flesch-Kincaid 66 vs 26 (p<0.001).
evidence.quote: AI summaries scored significantly higher for readability, comprehension, and usefulness than original reports (all p < 0.001), with equivalent trust ratings.

evidence.title: Training a Bilingual Artificial Intelligence Model on Pediatric Orthopaedic Resources to Enhance the Readability of Patient Education Materials
evidence.venue: Journal of the Pediatric Orthopaedic Society of North America
evidence.outcome: Readability grade level of AI-rewritten vs original pediatric orthopaedic patient education materials
evidence.effect: English Flesch-Kincaid grade 9.8 to 5.8 (P<.001); Flesch Reading Ease 56.9 to 76.4; Spanish Fernández Huerta 81.0 to 100.7 (P<.001). 10 reviewed PEMs judged accurate.
evidence.quote: The AI model was able to significantly improve the readability of the PEMs in every formula used (Flesch Reading Ease: 76.4 vs 56.9, P < .0001; Flesch-Kincaid grade level: 5.8 vs 9.8, P < .0001; SMOG Index: 8.7 vs 11.8, P < .0001; Coleman Liau: 8.7 vs 11.6, P < .0001; Automated Readability Score: 7.8 vs 12.0, P < .0001; Dale-Chall Readability Score: 7.8 vs 8.8, P < .0001; Linsear Write Formula: 6.6 vs 10.7, P = <.0001; Gunning Fog: 7.1 vs 10.8, P < .0001).

evidence.title: Comparison of AI chatbot-generated and web-based health information on the effects of radiation in fetuses and children
evidence.outcome: understandability of patient education text
evidence.effect: PEMAT-P understandability ≥70: web 7.5%; normal ChatGPT-4o 50.0%, Gemini 78.6%; 6th-grade ChatGPT variants and Gemini 100.0%, Copilot 26.7%.
evidence.quote: For the proportion of texts with PEMAT-P Understandability scores ≥70, ChatGPT-4o (n=7, 50.0%) and Gemini (n=11, 78.6%) at the Normal level, and ChatGPT-4o (n=15, 100.0%), ChatGPT-4o mini (n=15, 100.0%), ChatGPT-o1 (n=15, 100.0%), ChatGPT-o1 mini (n=15, 100.0%), and Gemini (n=14, 100.0%) at the 6th grade level showed significantly higher proportions compared to other groups ( P <0.05).

evidence.title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Improve the Readability of German Online Medical Texts: Evaluation Study
evidence.outcome: Readability (WSTF, FRE) of LLM-simplified German patient education texts versus originals and eighth-grade target
evidence.effect: Original WSTF 11.24, FRE 35.92. Copilot WSTF 8.99, GPT-3.5 9.96, GPT-4o 10.6 (significant improvement); Le Chat 11.71 (no improvement). No model significantly reached eighth-grade level.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-40, and Microsoft Copilot showed a statistically significant improvement in readability. However, the t tests yielded no statistically significant results for the reduction of scores lower than the eighth grade level.

evidence.title: Evaluating the efficacy of large language models in cardio-oncology patient education: a comparative analysis of accuracy, readability, and prompt engineering strategies
evidence.outcome: plain-language prompt tradeoff
evidence.effect: DouBao readability age decreased from 12.9 ± 0.8 to 10.1 ± 1.2 years (p<0.01), but accuracy decreased 57.5% to 7.5% (p<0.01).
evidence.quote: While simplifying language improves readability, it risks compromising clinical relevance.

evidence.title: A comparative evaluation of large language models for simplifying prostate cancer pathology reports: ChatGPT and Gemini
evidence.outcome: patient and clinician understandability
evidence.effect: Patient and clinician understandability ratings were consistently high across models; no numerical ratings reported.
evidence.quote: Patient and clinician understandability ratings were consistently high across models.

evidence.title: Enhancing readability and understandability of vascular surgery discharge summaries using artificial intelligence
evidence.outcome: Readability of AI-simplified versus original discharge summaries (Flesch-Kincaid grade level and ease score)
evidence.effect: 39.6% reduction in Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level and 106.37% increase in Ease Score; mean PEMAT-P understandability 77.71, actionability 52.12.
evidence.quote: AI-generated summaries demonstrated significant improvements in readability, with a 39.6% reduction in Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level and a 106.37% increase in Ease Score.

evidence.title: Optimizing Large Language Model Responses to Medical Queries: a Cross-sectional Study On the Effective Use of Chatgpt for Cancer-related Questions
evidence.outcome: Readability under a 6th-grade prompt
evidence.effect: 6th-grade prompt: ChatGPT-5 FKRE 64.92±8.56, FKGL 8.74±1.73, SMOG 6.97±1.26; ChatGPT-4o FKRE 65.44±7.43, FKGL 8.73±1.80, SMOG 6.86±1.53.
evidence.quote: The 6th-grade prompt markedly improved readability over other strategies (ChatGPT-5: FKRE:64.92 ± 8.56, GFI:8.10 ± 1.13, FKGL:8.74 ± 1.73, SMOG:6.97 ± 1.26; ChatGPT-4o:65.44 ± 7.43, GFI:8.04 ± 1.48, FKGL:8.73 ± 1.80, SMOG:6.86 ± 1.53).

evidence.title: Simplifying radiology reports with large language models: privacy-compliant open- versus closed-weight models
evidence.outcome: Flesch reading ease and layperson understandability of LLM-simplified versus original radiology reports
evidence.effect: Flesch reading ease: GPT-4o 46±7, Llama-3-70b 44±6, Mixtral-8x22B 44±6 vs original 17±13 (p<0.001); understandability 4.1-4.4 vs 1.5 (p<0.001).
evidence.quote: All three LLM reports yielded markedly higher layperson-understandability ratings than the original reports (GPT-4o: 4.4 ± 0.1; Llama-3-70B: 4.3 ± 0.1; Mixtral-8x22B: 4.1 ± 0.1 vs. 1.5 ± 0.1; p < 0.001 for each), with no significant difference between GPT-4o and Llama-3-70B (p = 0.136).

evidence.title: Guidelines vs. generative AI in CKD patient education: the role of prompt engineering and expert blinded evaluation
evidence.outcome: Readability (FKGL, FRE) of LLM CKD responses with structured plain-language prompt vs unstructured prompt
evidence.effect: Structured prompt lowered FKGL from 11.34 to 7.87 (ChatGPT) and 9.62 to 7.13 (Gemini); FRE rose to 64.23 and 61.45; p < 0.001.
evidence.quote: Providing a structured prompt made the responses of both models significantly easier to read and reduced the required educational level to below high school (7th grade level).

evidence.title: Impact of GPT-4-Generated Discharge Letters on Patients' Medical Comprehension: Prospective Crossover Study
evidence.outcome: Comprehension of safety-relevant discharge information: GPT-4 patient-centered letters versus standard discharge letters
evidence.effect: OR 1.74 (95% CI 1.45-2.08; P<.001). Learning objectives fully stated 45.7% vs 38.5%; omissions 24.3% vs 34.8%. Gains were largest for medication and organization, smaller for higher-order understanding.
evidence.quote: The letter type significantly influenced comprehension (odds ratio [OR] 1.74, 95% CI 1.45-2.08; P<.001).

evidence.title: A Blinded Analysis of Quality and Fidelity in Orthopaedic Patient Education Materials Simplified by ChatGPT and Humans
evidence.venue: The Journal of bone and joint surgery. American volume
evidence.outcome: Reading grade level of PEMs after ChatGPT-4o plain-language simplification
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4o-simplified PEMs had mean reading grade levels of 6.1 in English and 3.5 in Spanish, with acceptable fidelity.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4o-simplified PEMs showed mean reading grade levels of 6.1 in English and 3.5 in Spanish.
evidence.sample_unit: orthopaedic patient education documents (86 with human easy-to-read versions used for fidelity analysis)

evidence.title: Comparing the Readability and Content Quality of Online Patient Education Materials and ChatGPT-Generated Patient Education Materials for Breast Cancer Surgery and Reconstruction
evidence.outcome: Readability (FKGL) of patient education materials with vs without plain-language sixth-grade prompting
evidence.effect: Median FKGL 10.0 for standard ChatGPT vs 5.8 for simplified ChatGPT (p<0.001); simplified aligned with sixth-grade level (p=0.19); DISCERN quality did not differ (p=0.083).
evidence.quote: Pairwise testing showed that the median FKGL of simplified ChatGPT responses was significantly lower than that of OPEMs ( p < 0.001) and of standard ChatGPT responses ( p < 0.001), indicating an increased ease of readability in simplified ChatGPT responses ( Fig. 1 and Table 1 ).
evidence.sample_unit: patient education materials (99 online web sites, 60 ChatGPT responses)

evidence.title: Self-reported comprehension of large language model-generated summaries of lung cancer screening reports: a vignette survey
evidence.outcome: Comprehension and anxiety with vs without LLM patient-friendly summary of lung cancer screening reports
evidence.effect: Adding a patient summary improved objective comprehension (P<.001) and reduced anxiety (P<.001) in all scenarios; gains were larger for low self-rated English literacy (comprehension P<.001; anxiety P=.012) and health literacy (anxiety P<.001).
evidence.quote: LLM-generated PS of lung cancer screening reports increase comprehension and reduce anxiety, most notably among individuals with lower self-rated English and health literacy.

evidence.title: Evaluating large language models for simplifying non-English medical consent with clinician involvement
evidence.outcome: layperson comprehension
evidence.effect: Average score increased from 2.64 (SD = 0.57) to 3.53 (SD = 0.38), p = 0.008.
evidence.quote: In contrast, layperson comprehension improved significantly, with the average score increasing from 2.64 (SD = 0.57) to 3.53 (SD = 0.38), p = 0.008.
evidence.sample_unit: informed consent documents (each in 3 versions, rated by 4 surgeons and 4 laypersons)

evidence.title: Multidimensional evaluation of large language models in radiology report readability
evidence.outcome: Patient subjective and objective comprehension of LLM-simplified vs original reports
evidence.effect: Subjective comprehension 3.59±0.74 to 4.68±0.47; objective 1.64±0.84 to 2.78±0.42 (P<0.05); STAI-6 anxiety 16.74 to 10.44 in 800 patients
evidence.quote: The results of clinical setting validation showed that, compared with the original radiology reports (subjective comprehension scores: 3.59 ± 0.74；objective comprehension scores: 1.64 ± 0.84), reading the reports simplified by DeepSeek-R1 significantly improved patients’ subjective comprehension scores (4.68 ± 0.47; P < 0.05; r = 0.91；95%CI:0.89–0.92) and objective comprehension scores (2.78 ± 0.42; P < 0.05; r = 0.90；95%CI:0.88–0.91).
evidence.sample_unit: radiology reports (plus 800 patients in clinical setting validation)

evidence.title: Optimizing ChatGPT Applying prompt engineering to frequently asked questions in urologic oncology
evidence.venue: Canadian Urological Association journal = Journal de l'Association des urologues du Canada
evidence.outcome: Readability, understandability and actionability of ChatGPT patient education responses before vs after prompt engineering
evidence.effect: Grade reading level 10.5 to 5.3 (p<0.0001); reading ease 42 to 71.7 (p<0.0001); PEMAT-P understandability 88.4-95.5%; actionability 25.6-84.2%; DISCERN 3.42-4.47.
evidence.quote: Using prompt engineering, DISCERN (3.42-4.47, p<0.0001), PEMAT-P understandability (88.4-95.5%, p<0.0001), actionability (25.6-84.2%, p<0.0001), grade reading level (10.5-5.3, p<0.0001), and reading level (42 [college level] to 71.7 [7th grade], p<0.0001), all significantly improved.

evidence.title: Enhancing Readability of Surgical Patient Education Resources Using ChatGPT
evidence.outcome: Readability (SMOG) of ChatGPT-simplified surgical patient education materials versus originals
