evidence.effect: Mean SMOG decreased from 12.1 to 10.5 (P < 10^-9); Flesch-Kincaid -1.6; Coleman-Liau -0.8; sixth-grade level still hard to reach.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4o simplification significantly decreased mean Simple Measure of Gobbledygook score from 12.1 to 10.5 (P < 10<sup>-9</sup>), with similar reductions in Coleman-Liau index (-0.8, P < 10<sup>-5</sup>) and Flesch-Kincaid (-1.6, P < 10<sup>-8</sup>).

evidence.title: Improving the Readability of Spasmodic Dysphonia Patient Education Materials Using ChatGPT-4o Mini: A Cross-Sectional Study
evidence.venue: Journal of voice : official journal of the Voice Foundation
evidence.outcome: Readability gains and content fidelity of AI plain-language revision of patient education materials
evidence.effect: Readability improved significantly, but of 407 statement pairs 57% dropped content, 29% reduced specificity; 21% of PEMs fully preserved, 50% partial, 29% not preserved.
evidence.quote: Overall, 21% of PEMs were fully preserved (F), 50% were partially preserved (P), and 29% were not preserved (X), primarily due to omission of clinical detail or reduced specificity.

evidence.title: Evaluation of large language models in generating and optimizing educational materials for neonatal home oxygen therapy
evidence.outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of AI-rewritten patient education versus human-authored originals
evidence.effect: All 6 models' rewritten texts had significantly higher understandability than originals (p<0.01); median rose from 78.5 to 87.0-100.0.
evidence.quote: The median understandability of original texts was 78.5, while AI-rewritten texts improved to between 87.0 and 100.0.

evidence.title: Improving patient understanding of oncology imaging: radiologist and patient evaluation of summarised versus full-length AI-simplified reports from a tertiary cancer centre
evidence.venue: Cancer imaging : the official publication of the International Cancer Imaging Society
evidence.outcome: Patient-facing readability and perceived benefit
evidence.effect: PPI accessibility median: original 1.667 (0% >4), A 4.333 (60% >4), B 4.333 (85% ≥4); overall P<0.0001.
evidence.quote: In all questions, combined colorectal and lung cohorts, the Friedman test showed significant differences between the original version, version A, and version B reports (all P < 0.0001), with the original scoring less for accessibility and being beneficial to patients, in comparison with versions A and B as per Table 4 .
evidence.sample_unit: original CT oncology reports (30 colorectal, 30 lung), each simplified into two versions and rated by radiologists and PPI readers

evidence.title: Assessing ChatGPT vs. evidence-based online responses for polycystic ovary syndrome self-management and education: an international cross-sectional blinded survey of healthcare professionals
evidence.outcome: Change in readability scores after prompting ChatGPT to simplify responses
evidence.effect: Simplified answers improved: FRE 41.95 to 57.77, FKGL 12.60 to 8.55, GFI 12.93 to 10.63, ARI 15.35 to 11.20 (p<0.01 for all versus evidence-based).
evidence.quote: Accordingly, all readability scores improved significantly for the ChatGPT simplified answers ( p < 0.01 for all analyses) ( Table 4 ).
evidence.country: International (14 countries: Italy, Austria, Germany, UK, Switzerland, Canada, USA, Australia, and others)

evidence.title: Speaking Patient's Language: Assessment of Readability and Fidelity of Artificial Intelligence-Optimized Consent Forms
evidence.outcome: Readability of LLM-rewritten consent forms versus originals
evidence.effect: First LLM revision improved readability to an 8.8 ± 1.2 grade level (P < 0.01), a five-grade reduction; second revision showed no further improvement (9.9 ± 1.2; P = 0.87).
evidence.quote: First LLM revision significantly improved readability to an 8.8 ± 1.2 grade level (P < 0.01), a five-grade reduction.

evidence.title: Enhancing Health Literacy in Endourology: Using Artificial Intelligence to Improve Readability of Patient Education Materials
evidence.outcome: Readability of AI-rewritten patient education materials versus originals across six indices
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4o reduced reading level by about four grade levels to fourth to sixth grade (p<0.001 all indices); e.g., FKG 9.72 to 4.93, FRE 55.75 to 76.62. Comprehension not tested.
evidence.quote: Overall, GPT-4o reduced the reading level of all 21 PEMs by approximately four grade levels and brought them into alignment with national recommendations for patient-facing content.

evidence.title: Unlikely Storyteller: Leveraging Narrative-Based Communication in LLM-Generated Medical Advice
evidence.outcome: Terminology explanation frequency per reply across clinician, unprompted AI, and prompted AI
evidence.effect: Terminology explanations per reply: clinician 0.301, unprompted AI 1.337, prompted AI 1.981; replies with no explanation fell from 81.1% (clinician) to 38.3% (unprompted) to 15.3% (prompted).
evidence.quote: With the narrative prompt, explanation density increased further to 1.981 (95% CI [1.901, 2.061]), while the share of replies offering no explanation fell to 15.3% (Wilson 95% CI [0.132, 0.177]).

evidence.title: Improving Readability of Stroke Clinical Trial Consent Forms Using Artificial Intelligence
evidence.outcome: Readability of AI-edited consent materials versus originals, with semantic similarity
evidence.effect: Flesch-Kincaid grade 11.52 original vs 9.47 GPT-edited (P<0.001); mean semantic similarity 0.85 (SD=0.04).
evidence.quote: Mean reading levels were 11.52 for the original and 9.47 for the GPT-edited ICFs using the Flesch-Kincaid grade level (P<0.001).

evidence.title: Plain-language prompting improves readability of ChatGPT-generated patient education for meniscal surgery without loss of accuracy
evidence.venue: Journal of ISAKOS : joint disorders & orthopaedic sports medicine
evidence.outcome: Readability (FKGL, FRES) of ChatGPT patient education before vs after plain-language prompt
evidence.effect: Plain-language prompt reduced FKGL by about 5 grade levels and raised FRES by 30-38 points (P < 0.001), with no loss of accuracy, relevance, or depth.
evidence.quote: The plain-language prompt significantly improved readability for both models, reducing FKGL by approximately 5 grade levels and increasing FRES by 30-38 points (P < 0.001), with no loss of accuracy, relevance, or depth.
evidence.sample_unit: standardized patient-focused questions (3 replicates each, two models)

evidence.title: A Comparison of a Customized Peripheral Artery Disease (PAD)-Specific Generative AI Chatbot and General-Purpose AI Chatbots for PAD Patient Education
evidence.outcome: Readability grade level of chatbot patient-education responses, plain-language customized vs general chatbots
evidence.effect: VERA (5th-grade system prompt) median FK grade 6.6 vs 7.5 ChatGPT, 9.0 Gemini, 8.0 Claude; Flesch Reading Ease 72 vs 52.5-57 (p<0.001 vs each). Comprehensiveness lower.
evidence.quote: VERA produced responses at a median grade level of 6.6 [4.7, 7.0] compared with 7.5 [6.2, 9.7] for ChatGPT, 9.0 [7.4, 10.2] for Gemini, and 8.0 [6.7, 9.0] for Claude.

evidence.title: Patient-friendly simplification and translation of neuroradiology impressions using artificial intelligence
evidence.outcome: Readability of radiology impressions before vs after LLM simplification
evidence.effect: Flesch-Kincaid Grade median 13.4 original vs 7.0 simplified (p<0.001, r=0.9); Flesch Reading Ease 23.3 vs 72.9; college level to middle-school level.
evidence.quote: On average, LLM-driven simplification brought reports from a college reading level to that of a middle schooler.
evidence.sample_unit: neuroradiology reports (brain MRI, head CT, spine MRI); 60 impressions translated to Spanish

evidence.title: Evaluation of Commonly Utilized Artificial Intelligence Large Language Models in Optimizing Readability, Accuracy, and Comprehension of Orthopaedic Oncology Patient Educational Materials
evidence.venue: The Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons
evidence.outcome: plain-language LLM rewrite readability
evidence.effect: All LLMs improved readability (P < 0.001); ChatGPT-4o, DeepSeek AI, and Google Gemini were most readable.
evidence.quote: All LLMs significantly improved readability (P < 0.001), and ChatGPT-4o, DeepSeek AI, and Google Gemini conversion produced the most readable outputs.

evidence.title: Feasibility of a multi-metric framework for evaluating patient-facing AI communication in cosmetic dentistry: an exploratory proof-of-concept study
evidence.outcome: Plain-language readability, practicality and structure of AI patient education responses with instruction configuration
evidence.effect: CSA-GPT had lower FKGL (6.07 vs 9.12), higher practicality (4.92 vs 4.45) and structural clarity (4.50 vs 3.19), all p < 0.001.
evidence.quote: Mean structural clarity scores were 4.50 ± 0.69 (95% CI: 4.35–4.65) for CSA-GPT and 3.19 ± 0.81 (95% CI: 3.01–3.37) for ChatGPT5.2 (all p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Large Language Model-Based Simplification of Digital Therapeutics Explanations for Insomnia and Nicotine Dependence: Two Randomized Online Experiments
evidence.outcome: Perceived understanding and ease, clarity, comprehensibility ratings of LLM-simplified vs original DTx materials
evidence.effect: Group×time interaction on perceived understanding: insomnia F=24.8, nicotine F=14.1 (both P<.001), greater gains with LLM-simplified text; ease/clarity/comprehensibility rated higher (r=0.11-0.24). Self-reported outcomes only.
evidence.quote: A significant group×time interaction was observed in both experiments.

evidence.title: Evaluating Large Language Models to Improve Spanish Patient Education on Childhood Glaucoma
evidence.venue: Journal of pediatric ophthalmology and strabismus
evidence.outcome: Readability and quality of LLM-simplified patient education materials in plain language
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4o improved readability from 56.6 ± 4.9 to 69.6 ± 2.3 (P < .001); quality stayed high (median 15 in both groups, P = .74); no hallucinations observed.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4o significantly improved readability to 69.6 ± 2.3 (4th- to 6th-grade level, P < .001).
evidence.sample_unit: Spanish-language patient educational materials on childhood glaucoma

evidence.title: Evaluating the Use of Large Language Models in Improving the Readability of Online Patient Education Materials for Peripheral Nerve Surgery
evidence.outcome: Readability of patient materials after LLM plain-language rewriting, with accuracy and comprehensiveness ratings
evidence.effect: FKGL fell from 11.3 to 7.5 with ChatGPT and 5.6 with Gemini (p<0.001). ChatGPT accuracy 4.5/5 vs Gemini 4.0/5; comprehensiveness 2.0/3 vs 1.0/3.
evidence.quote: The average FKGL of ChatGPT rewrites was significantly lower than that of OPEMs (11.3 vs. 7.5, p < 0.001), as was the average FKGL of Gemini rewrites (11.3 vs. 5.6, p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Natural Language Processing Improves Postoperative Discharge Instructions
evidence.venue: Arthroscopy : the journal of arthroscopic & related surgery : official publication of the Arthroscopy Association of North America and the International Arthroscopy Association
evidence.outcome: Readability, understandability and actionability of original versus ChatGPT plain-language rewritten discharge instructions
evidence.effect: Understandability rose from 63.6% to 87.9% (P < .001); actionability from 44.4% to 73.6% (P < .001); grade level fell from 9.8 to 7.5.
evidence.quote: Understandability and actionability scores improved from 63.6% to 87.9% (P < .001) and from 44.4% to 73.6%, respectively (P < .001).

evidence.title: Securing Safety and Quality in AI-generated Patient Education: A Nurse-led Methodological Framework Integrating Kolcaba's Comfort Theory
evidence.outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient education materials across iterative prompt refinement stages
evidence.effect: Readability scores significantly improved from 48.5 to 66.8 (Ateşman's Readability Index) after the three-stage nurse-led prompt process.
evidence.quote: Readability scores significantly improved from 48.5 to 66.8.
evidence.sample_unit: expert panel reviewers (evaluating AI-generated education materials for 3 disease cases)

evidence.title: Development and expert radiologist validation of a custom pipeline for simplification of oncology radiology reports using large language model
evidence.outcome: Readability of AI-simplified radiology reports (Flesch Reading Ease) versus original reports
evidence.effect: Readability improved markedly (Flesch Reading Ease 49.2→73); readability/tone rubric score 4.9 ± 0.32.
evidence.quote: Readability improved markedly (Flesch Reading Ease 49.2→73).

evidence.title: Large language model based simplification of ophthalmological clinical and ancillary results for patient readability
evidence.venue: International journal of retina and vitreous
evidence.outcome: readability after simplification
evidence.effect: All LLMs improved readability scores to varying degrees.
evidence.quote: All LLMs improved readability scores to varying degrees.

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Versus Professional Society Patient Education Materials in Gastroenterology, Surgery, Ophthalmology, and Anesthesiology: A Comparative Analysis of Readability and Health Literacy Metrics
evidence.outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid), quality, understandability, actionability of AI vs society patient materials by specialty
evidence.effect: Surgery: AI lower reading level and higher quality/understandability/actionability (p<0.001). Anesthesiology: AI more readable (p<0.001). Ophthalmology: AI more readable but society higher quality/understandability. Gastroenterology: AI higher reading level (p<0.001).
evidence.quote: In gastroenterology, AI materials had higher reading levels (p<0.001) with no differences in quality or usability.
evidence.sample_unit: paired patient education topics (25 per specialty)

evidence.title: The use of structured prompt to improve the readability, accuracy, and quality of ChatGPT responses on labor epidural analgesia: a brief report
evidence.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT labor epidural answers with vs without structured CRAFT prompt
evidence.effect: CRAFT responses ranged from 6th to 9th grade versus 9th grade to college level for direct questions; significantly better readability.
evidence.quote: Responses generated using CRAFT-based prompt had significantly better readability than those with direct questions only.

evidence.title: AI-powered radiology report simplification in Arabic: A prospective evaluation of patient-perceived understandability and clinical safety
evidence.outcome: Patient-perceived understandability of plain-language AI-simplified Arabic reports versus traditional radiologist reports (Likert 1-5)
evidence.effect: Median 1 (IQR 1-2) for AI-simplified Arabic vs 5 (IQR 3-5) for traditional reports (p<0.001; r=0.97); 94.9% (93/98) preferred the Arabic simplified version.
evidence.quote: AI-simplified Arabic reports produced a median perceived understandability score of 1 (IQR 1-2) versus 5 (IQR 3-5) for traditional reports (p < 0.001; rank-biserial r = 0.97), with 94.9% (93/98) of patients preferring the Arabic simplified version.

evidence.title: Improved Readability and Translational Instability in LLM-Generated Radiology Reports
evidence.outcome: radiology report readability
evidence.effect: LLMs significantly enhanced readability (P < 0.05); DeepSeek-R1 achieved the best performance.
evidence.quote: Overall, large language models significantly enhanced the readability of radiology reports (P < 0.05), with DeepSeek-R1 achieving the best performance.

evidence.title: Large Language Model Simplification of Open Access Pediatric Strabismus Literature: Cross-Sectional Validation of Readability and Clinical Fidelity
evidence.outcome: Readability (FKGL, SMOG) of LLM plain-language summaries versus original articles
evidence.effect: Mean FKGL fell from 15.79 (SD 1.53) to 7.84 (SD 1.30), difference 7.95 (95% CI 7.52-8.38; P<.001); SMOG fell from 14.41 to 7.68, difference 6.73.
evidence.quote: Following LLM processing, the mean FKGL score decreased significantly by 7.95 grade levels (95% CI 7.52-8.38; P <.001), and the mean SMOG score decreased by 6.73 grade levels (95% CI 6.42-7.04; P <.001).

evidence.title: Large language models versus expert clinicians in optimizing Chinese patient education materials for temporomandibular disorders: a mixed-methods study integrating readability, accuracy, actionability, and cultural adaptability
evidence.outcome: Actionability (PEMAT) of plain-language LLM-rewritten materials versus original and clinician-written materials
evidence.effect: LLM actionability 95.6% vs original 16.7% and clinician 46.7%; human-AI 95.6%; no human-written text reached the 70% threshold.
evidence.quote: All four LLM subgroups scored significantly higher than both A and C (all p ≤ 0.002): GPT-4 (80.0% ± 22.2%, 7/15 ≥ 70%), Claude Opus 4.6 (95.6% ± 11.3%, 13/15 ≥ 70%), DeepSeek-V2 (97.8% ± 8.6%, 14/15 ≥ 70%), Gemini 3.0 pro (95.6% ± 11.3%, 13/15 ≥ 70%).
evidence.sample_unit: education topics (60 texts in four-group analysis)

evidence.title: Prompting generative artificial intelligence to create plain language patient education materials
evidence.outcome: Understandability and actionability (PEMAT) of AI-generated patient education materials with plain-language prompt
evidence.effect: ChatGPT advanced prompt had 91% understandable and 84% actionable; advanced-prompt AIs exceeded the actionability threshold (>70%).
evidence.quote: All sources except HealthyChildren.org had mean understandability > 70%; AIs using the advanced prompt and UpToDate exceeded the actionability threshold.

evidence.title: Perceived inequalities and cultural inclusivity in UK Breast Cancer Information and Care: a mixed method study
evidence.outcome: Readability of clinician-developed, LLM-assisted leaflet versus existing leaflets
evidence.effect: The LLM-assisted leaflet met ages 12-13, closer to recommended 9-11 (FRES +7.72; FKGL -1.96; GFI -2.24; SMOG -1.4; CLI -0.39).
evidence.quote: The clinician developed, LLM assisted leaflet met ages 12-13, closer to national recommended levels of 9-11.
evidence.sample_unit: survey respondents (medical students and resident doctors); 239 NHS trusts' leaflets reviewed

evidence.title: Rethinking Pediatric Asthma Education Through Large Language Model Generation and Simplification: Randomized Double-Blind Study
evidence.outcome: Perceived quality and usefulness of LLM-simplified plain-language patient education versus expert-authored
evidence.effect: AI-SRs vs PEARs total scores not significantly different in either group (mean difference 0.01 for professionals, 1.29 for families; Holm-adjusted P>.99), though word count and difficult words decreased.
evidence.quote: Additional language simplification did not improve acceptance in this predominantly highly educated sample, and the strong tendency to attribute materials to human authors highlights the importance of source transparency.

evidence.title: Validation of an AI-powered mobile application for personalizing medical note explanations: a mixed-methods evaluation
evidence.outcome: Readability of AI explanations versus original clinician notes (FK grade, Flesch Reading Ease, Gunning Fog)
evidence.effect: FK Grade Level fell 10.57 to 7.61; Flesch Reading Ease rose 37.7 to 69.6; Gunning Fog fell 14.5 to 10.4; all P ≤ 0.002.
evidence.quote: AI-generated explanations demonstrated consistent improvements in readability, with mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level decreasing by 2.96 levels (10.57-7.61), Flesch Reading Ease increasing by 31.9 points (37.7-69.6), and Gunning Fog Index decreasing by 4.09 points (14.5-10.4); all improvements were statistically significant (all P ≤ 0.002).
evidence.sample_unit: AI-generated explanations (plus 15 expert reviewers and 54 patient survey participants)

evidence.title: Online patient information on elective orthognathic surgery provided by UK National Health Services hospitals: assessment of readability and improvement using large language models
evidence.venue: The British journal of oral & maxillofacial surgery
evidence.outcome: Readability of LLM-simplified patient leaflets against NHS standards across five indices
evidence.effect: All three LLMs significantly improved readability across all indices (p<0.001); Gemini met targets on 3/5 indices; no model consistently met all NHS standards.
evidence.quote: Despite significant improvements, no model consistently met all NHS standards.

evidence.title: Comprehension of an AI-generated discharge letter versus a traditional discharge letter: two controlled quasi-experimental parallel-group studies
evidence.venue: International journal for quality in health care : journal of the International Society for Quality in Health Care
evidence.outcome: Comprehension of key discharge information: AI accessibility-optimised letter vs conventional letter
evidence.effect: Comprehension scores were higher with the AI letter in Study 1 (median 4 vs 2) and Study 2 (median 4 vs 3), both P<0.001. All secondary outcomes also improved; no gain for follow-up date identification.
evidence.quote: Participants receiving the AI-generated discharge letter achieved significantly higher comprehension scores in both studies (Study 1: median 4 vs. 2; Study 2: median 4 vs. 3; both P < 0.001).

evidence.title: Improving patient communication and understanding of medical reports through text simplification with ChatGPT: a comparative study
evidence.outcome: Lay participants' comprehension accuracy and ratings of simplified versus original medical reports
evidence.effect: Simplified reports rated higher for clarity, structure, and usefulness (p<0.001); comprehension improved (e.g., MRI 80.3% vs 53.7%; p<0.001); FRE 48.4 vs 22.9.
evidence.quote: Across all document types, patients rated simplified texts significantly higher in clarity, structure, and usefulness (p < 0.001), with significantly improved comprehension accuracy (e.g., MRI 80.3% vs. 53.7%; p < 0.001).

evidence.title: MedReadCtrl: Personalizing medical text generation with readability-controlled instruction learning
evidence.outcome: Readability instruction-following error and expert preference for readability-controlled versus GPT-4 outputs
evidence.effect: MedReadCtrl had lower readability instruction-following error than GPT-4 (1.39 vs. 1.59 on ReadMe, p<0.001). Experts preferred MedReadCtrl 71.7% vs. 23.3%, especially at low literacy levels.
evidence.quote: MedReadCtrl achieves significantly lower readability instruction-following errors than GPT-4 (e.g., 1.39 vs. 1.59 on ReadMe, p<0.001)

evidence.title: A Reproducible Framework for Safe LLM-Based Simplification of ICU Discharge Summaries in Clinical Information Systems
evidence.outcome: readability of simplified discharge summaries
evidence.effect: Flesch Reading Ease increased from 51.2 ± 6.1 to 58.3–60.3; grade level decreased from 9.4 ± 1.2 to 7.6–8.0.
evidence.quote: All six prompting conditions significantly improved readability versus the original notes (all p < 0.0001), increasing Flesch Reading Ease from 51.2 ± 6.1 to 58.3–60.3 and reducing grade level from 9.4 ± 1.2 to 7.6–8.0.
evidence.sample_unit: ICU discharge summaries (MIMIC-III notes); 60 notes for blinded human review

evidence.title: Utilizing Large Language Models to Simplify Radiology Reports: a comparative analysis of ChatGPT3.5, ChatGPT4.0, Google Bard, and Microsoft Bing
evidence.outcome: Readability indices of radiology reports before versus after LLM simplification under three prompts
evidence.effect: All four LLMs significantly simplified 254 reports on four readability indices; performance varied by prompt and model, and ChatGPT models did best with added context such as a 7th grade target.
evidence.quote: All LLMs significantly simplified the reports, but performance varied based on the prompt used and the specific model.

evidence.title: Comparison of ChatGPT and Traditional Patient Education Materials for Men's Health
evidence.outcome: readability after sixth-grade prompt
evidence.effect: Adjusted ChatGPT readability typically surpassed UCF and met the recommended level for 2 topics.
evidence.quote: Conversely, adjusted ChatGPT readability typically surpassed UCF, even meeting the recommended level for 2 topics.
evidence.sample_unit: men's health topics (UCF resources compared with ChatGPT responses)

evidence.title: Can Artificial Intelligence Improve the Readability of Patient Education Materials on Aortic Stenosis? A Pilot Study
evidence.outcome: Readability of LLM-rewritten patient education materials versus originals
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-3.5 improved all four measures (FRE 76.9 vs 51.9, p<0.001), reaching ~6th-7th grade; Bard improved three of four (FRE 66.5), ~8th-9th grade; neither reached below 6th grade.
evidence.quote: Conversion of PEMs by ChatGPT-3.5 demonstrated significantly improved mean readability scores across all four validated measures: FRE (76.9 ± 1.2 vs 51.9 ± 11.6, p < 0.001), FKGL (5.9 ± 0.8 vs 9.4 ± 2.0, p < 0.001), GFI (7.7 ± 0.9 vs 11.3 ± 2.1, p < 0.001), and SMOGI (8.8 ± 0.6 vs 10.1 ± 1.2, p < 0.001) scores, indicating fairly easy readability at the approximately 6th–7th grade reading level.

evidence.title: Validation of ChatGPT 3.5 as a Tool to Optimize Readability of Patient-facing Craniofacial Education Materials
evidence.venue: Plastic and reconstructive surgery. Global open
evidence.outcome: Reading grade level of ChatGPT-simplified patient education text versus originals
evidence.effect: Simplified excerpts mean grade level 7.78 by calculator (7.69 by ChatGPT), significantly lower than originals (P < 0.001) and below the recommended maximum of 8.
evidence.quote: The mean grade level for the simplified excerpts with the traditional readability calculator was 7.78.

evidence.title: Large language models and bariatric surgery patient education: a comparative readability analysis of GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Bard, and online institutional resources
evidence.outcome: Readability change after prompting LLM to explain in simpler terms
evidence.effect: Simplified responses had significantly higher FRE and lower grade levels than initial for all LLMs (p<0.05); GPT-4 FRE 42.7 to 74.0, reading levels 6th to 9th grade.
evidence.quote: Simplified responses from GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and Bard received higher FRE scores, as well as lower grade levels across all instruments, compared to those of initial responses from GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and Bard, respectively ( p < 0.05) (Table 3 , Supplementary Table 7).

evidence.title: An artificial intelligence language model improves readability of burns first aid information
evidence.venue: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
evidence.outcome: Readability of burns first aid materials before and after AI rewriting to an 11-year-old literacy level
evidence.effect: Original: 4% met target on all tools, median grade 6.9. After AI: 18% met target, median grade 6 (p<.001); all readability scores improved significantly (p<.001).
evidence.quote: Once rewritten using AI, paired t-test demonstrated that all readability scores improved significantly (p < .001).

evidence.title: Quantitative Evaluation of Large Language Models to Streamline Radiology Report Impressions: A Multimodal Retrospective Analysis
evidence.outcome: Readability grade level of simplified impressions
evidence.effect: All four LLMs simplified impressions across all prompts tested (P < .001).
evidence.quote: All four LLMs simplified radiology report impressions across all prompts tested (P < .001).

evidence.title: Biomedical text readability after hypernym substitution with fine-tuned large language models
evidence.outcome: Readability and sentence complexity of biomedical text before vs after LLM hypernym substitution
evidence.effect: All three fine-tuned LLM approaches improved readability and sentence complexity; scores moved from collegiate to US high-school level; GPT-J-6b best on sentence complexity.
evidence.quote: Readability scores were translated from a pre-processed collegiate reading level to a post-processed US high-school level.

evidence.title: Enhancing Readability of Online Patient-Facing Content: The Role of AI Chatbots in Improving Cancer Information Accessibility
evidence.venue: Journal of the National Comprehensive Cancer Network : JNCCN
evidence.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT-rewritten cancer content versus original, with accuracy and quality
evidence.effect: Readability fell from grade 13±1.5 to grade 9±0.8; F1 0.87, cosine similarity 0.915; DISCERN 28.5±5 with no significant difference from originals.
evidence.quote: However, after ChatGPT's intervention, the AI-generated outputs had a mean readability score equivalent to a high school freshman education level (grade 9±0.8).

evidence.title: Enhancing readability of USFDA patient communications through large language models: a proof-of-concept study
evidence.outcome: Readability of LLM-simplified materials versus originals, with technical accuracy retained
evidence.effect: LLMs reduced grade levels (single prompt DSCs: ChatGPT 10.1, Gemini 8; MGs: ChatGPT 7.1, Gemini 6.5); outputs retained technical accuracy and key messages.
evidence.quote: LLMs significantly improved readability, reducing the grade levels to more accessible readings (Single prompt - DSCs: ChatGPT 4.0© 10.1, Gemini© 8; MGs: ChatGPT 4.0© 7.1, Gemini© 6.5.
evidence.sample_unit: FDA drug safety communications and medication guides

evidence.title: Can Generative Artificial Intelligence Enhance Health Literacy About Lateral Epicondylitis?
evidence.outcome: Readability of patient education materials after generative AI plain-language rewriting
evidence.effect: All rewritten PEMs scored below eighth-grade level; average readability 6.12 ± 0.97 versus 9.81 ± 1.76 originally; word count fell from 600.68 to 253.96.
evidence.quote: Following ChatGPT’s edits to the original PEMs, all 25 rewritten PEMs obtained average readability scores below the eighth-grade reading level.
evidence.sample_unit: institutional patient education materials on lateral epicondylitis

evidence.title: Assessing AI Simplification of Medical Texts: Readability and Content Fidelity
evidence.outcome: Readability (FKGL, FKRE) of texts before and after GPT-4 plain-language simplification
evidence.effect: FKGL decreased from 12th to 5th grade for abstracts and 13th to 5th for PEMs (p < 0.001); FKRE showed similar improvement (p < 0.001).
evidence.quote: FKGL decreased from 12th to 5th grade for abstracts and 13th to 5th for PEMs (p < 0.001).
evidence.sample_unit: texts (100 abstracts and 340 patient education materials)

evidence.title: Improving readability in AI-generated medical information on fragility fractures: the role of prompt wording on ChatGPT's responses
evidence.venue: Osteoporosis international : a journal established as result of cooperation between the European Foundation for Osteoporosis and the National Osteoporosis Foundation of the USA
evidence.outcome: Readability and grade level of AI medical responses
evidence.effect: Plain-language prompts FKRE median 34.35 vs 23.60; FKGL median 12.05 vs 14.50; both statistically significant.
evidence.quote: The FKRE scores indicated significantly higher readability with plain language prompts (median 34.35) compared to keyword-only prompts (median 23.60).
evidence.sample_unit: keywords (each tested with two prompt types)

evidence.title: Source Characteristics Influence AI-Enabled Orthopaedic Text Simplification: Recommendations for the Future
evidence.outcome: Readability (FKRE, FKGL) of orthopaedic patient education materials before vs after LLM simplification
evidence.effect: All LLMs improved FKRE and FKGL (p < 0.01); GPT-4 transformed PEMs to a seventh-grade reading level (mean FKGL 6.72 ± 0.99), outperforming other models.
evidence.quote: All LLMs improved FKRE and FKGL scores (p < 0.01).

evidence.title: Enhancing Patient Comprehension of Glomerular Disease Treatments Using ChatGPT
evidence.outcome: Readability and PEMAT understandability of GPT-4 explanations, general vs prompted for 8th-grade level
evidence.effect: Grade level fell from 12.85 ± 0.93 to 8.44 ± 0.72; FRE rose from 25.73 to 60.75; PEMAT understandability rose from 60.7% to 76.8% (p<0.0001).
evidence.quote: Furthermore, we performed a PEMAT analysis to evaluate understandability ( Table 4 ), which demonstrated a notable enhancement in the understandability scores, increasing from 60.70 ± 8.46 for general explanations to 76.82 ± 11.39 for tailored explanations.
evidence.sample_unit: glomerular disease terms (paired general and tailored GPT-4 explanations)

evidence.title: Tailoring glaucoma education using large language models: Addressing health disparities in patient comprehension
evidence.outcome: Readability of glaucoma texts before versus after GPT-4 simplification (FKGL, FKRE)
evidence.effect: Abstracts: FKGL fell 3.21 points (30%, P<.001), FKRE rose 28.6 points (66%, P<.001). PEMs: FKGL fell 2.38 points (28%, P=.0272), FKRE rose 12.14 points (19%, P=.0459). Cosine similarity 0.861 for abstracts, 0.937 for PEMs.
evidence.quote: The transformation of abstracts resulted in FKGL decreasing by an average of 3.21 points (30%, P < .001) and FKRE increasing by 28.6 points (66%, P < .001).
evidence.sample_unit: documents (62 journal abstracts and 9 patient education materials)

evidence.title: ChatGPT 3.5 Better Improves Comprehensibility of English, than Spanish, Generated Responses to Osteosarcoma Questions
evidence.outcome: Change in readability after asking ChatGPT to 'Make text easier to understand'
evidence.effect: English FRES 51.8 to 63.3 and FKGL 10.51 to 8.27; Spanish FRES 51.6 to 66.1 and FKGL 10.29 to 7.2 (all p<0.001), though simplified text remained above 5th-6th grade level.
evidence.quote: While the modifications significantly improved the readability within each respective language, when comparing between English and Spanish it was better at modifying English responses.

evidence.title: Readability of Orthopaedic Patient Educational Material: An artificial intelligence application
evidence.venue: Journal of clinical orthopaedics and trauma
evidence.outcome: Plain-language readability of AI-rewritten patient education materials versus originals
evidence.effect: All GPT models lowered mean combined grade level; rewritten articles screened with no falsified information or medical inaccuracies.
evidence.quote: AI is a viable option for reducing the reading difficulty of patient educational materials while maintaining accuracy.

evidence.title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Enhance Patient Educational Resources in Rhinology
evidence.venue: The Annals of otology, rhinology, and laryngology
evidence.outcome: Readability of LLM-rewritten patient education materials versus originals (FKGL, FKRE)
evidence.effect: LLM-generated PEMs had significantly better readability (mean FKGL 8.6 vs 10.28, P<.0001); Gemini best with FKGL 7.5 and FKRE 65.5, though not reaching sixth grade.
evidence.quote: LLMs improved the readability of PEMs, potentially enhancing accessibility to medical information for diverse populations.

evidence.title: Promoting patient health literacy in burn care through artificial intelligence language learning models: A study of text analysis and simplification
evidence.venue: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
evidence.outcome: Readability grade level of burn care patient materials after AI simplification, versus 6th-8th grade target
evidence.effect: Microsoft Copilot, Gemini, and Meta AI reduced readability scores to within the 6th to 8th-grade level. ChatGPT 4o is not reported as reaching the target. Clinician oversight is still needed for accuracy.
evidence.quote: Additionally, when tasked with simplifying the texts, Microsoft Copilot, Gemini, and Meta AI reduced the readability scores to within the desired 6th to 8th-grade level.

evidence.title: Bridging Health Literacy Gaps in Spine Care: Using ChatGPT-4o to Improve Patient-Education Materials
evidence.venue: The Journal of bone and joint surgery. American volume
evidence.outcome: Readability of patient education materials after AI plain-language rewriting versus originals
evidence.effect: Mean FKGL fell from 10.2 ± 2.6 to 6.6 ± 1.3 (p < 0.05) while reportedly maintaining accuracy and adequate detail; test-retest ICC 0.91 to 0.98.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4o demonstrated the potential to enhance PEM readability while maintaining content quality.

evidence.title: Currently Available Large Language Models Are Moderately Effective in Improving Readability of English and Spanish Patient Education Materials in Pediatric Orthopaedics
evidence.venue: The Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons
evidence.outcome: Proportion of AI-rewritten patient education materials reaching sixth-grade reading level or below
evidence.effect: Baseline ≤sixth FKGL was 5.8% English and 10.0% Spanish. After ChatGPT-4.0/Gemini, English 21.4%/60.2%; Spanish 52.5%/77.5% achieved ≤sixth FKGL.
evidence.quote: 21.4% and 60.2% of ChatGPT-4.0-converted and Google Gemini-converted English PEMs achieved ≤sixth FKGL, respectively.

evidence.title: Implementing Generative AI to Enhance Patient Education on Retinopathy of Prematurity
evidence.venue: Journal of pediatric ophthalmology and strabismus
evidence.outcome: PEM understandability, quality, and accuracy
evidence.effect: median DISCERN = 4; PEMAT-U ≥ 70%; Likert = 1.
evidence.quote: LLM-generated PEMs were of high quality (median DISCERN = 4), understandable (PEMAT-U ≥ 70%), and accurate (Likert = 1).

evidence.title: Using AI to Translate and Simplify Spanish Orthopedic Medical Text: Instrument Validation Study
evidence.outcome: Readability of LLM-simplified Spanish orthopedic patient education materials versus originals, relative to target grade level
evidence.effect: Simplified PEMs had improved readability versus originals (P<.001) but did not reach the targeted grade level; GPT-4 also significantly reduced complexity of Spanish medical text (P<.001).
evidence.quote: Simplified PEMs demonstrated improved readability when compared to original versions (P<.001) but were unable to reach the targeted grade level for simplification.

evidence.title: ChatGPT-4 in Neurosurgery: Improving Patient Education Materials
evidence.outcome: readability and accuracy of rewritten patient education materials

evidence.quote: The mean FRE score for rewritten PEMs on each topic were significantly lower than nonrewritten materials ( P < .01) except spinal stenosis ( P = .104) and were validated for accuracy.

evidence.title: Enhancing the Readability of Online Pediatric Cataract Education Materials: A Comparative Study of Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: Reading grade level of patient education materials before vs after LLM simplification
evidence.effect: Average reading level fell from 10.59 ± 2.20 to 8.44 ± 1.84 (ChatGPT-4o), 7.50 ± 2.10 (Gemini 2.0), and 7.01 ± 0.91 (DeepSeek-R1), P < 0.001.
evidence.quote: After LLM conversion, the readability improved significantly, with the average reading level reduced to 8.44 ± 1.84 using ChatGPT-4o, 7.50 ± 2.10 with Gemini 2.0, and 7.01 ± 0.91 with DeepSeek-R1 ( P < 0.001 ).

evidence.title: Prompt Engineering and Follow-Up Questioning Improves the Readability of Spine Surgery Questions in Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: Readability of LLM spine surgery answers under different plain-language prompting strategies
evidence.effect: Phase 2 (sixth-grade level request) gave the most readable responses, with 51.11% meeting the sixth-grade level. Follow-up clarification and simple prompts beat complex rule-based prompts.
evidence.quote: Phase 2 yielded the most readable responses, with 51.11% meeting the sixth-grade level.

evidence.title: Self-Reflective Chest X-Ray Report Generation with Clinical-Aware Detection and Multilevel Readability
evidence.outcome: Patient comprehension score of AI-generated radiology reports adapted to plain-language reading levels
evidence.effect: 56.88% increase in patient comprehension scores reported, alongside 19.78% AUROC gain, 17.29% mAP improvement, and 5.26% gain in diagnostic precision (benchmark datasets, automated evaluation).

evidence.title: ChatGPT as a tool to improve readability of rheumatology patient education materials: a positive start with significant hurdles
evidence.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT-simplified patient education materials versus original and 6th grade target
evidence.effect: ChatGPT lowered mean reading level from 12.02 to 9.35 ± 1.12 (range grades 7-13) but failed to reach 6th grade level.

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence Simplification of English and Spanish Surgical Consent Forms: 1-Size Does Not Fit All

evidence.effect: English improved modestly with ChatGPT-4.0 and more with custom GPT; Spanish direct simplification did not significantly improve (GPM 9.5 to 10.0; SOL 9.6 to 9.1; both p > 0.05).

evidence.title: Effectiveness of ChatGPT in simplifying information for Polish patients on cervical cancer screening using advanced prompting

evidence.quote: Prompting LLMs to produce PEMs at a 5th-grade level consistently produced statistically lower readability scores than unprompted outputs.

evidence.title: Readability of Retina Patient Education Materials Generated With a Large Language Model

evidence.title: Bridging the Health Literacy Gap for Patients With Oral Cancer: Readability Enhancement With AI Chatbots

evidence.title: Transformation of Home Physical Therapy Guidance with Generative AI

evidence.outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid) of home physical therapy guidance with vs without generative AI and prompt design

evidence.quote: The Flesch-Kincaid index was employed for testing the guidelines complexity and readability, showing how appropriate prompts sent to the API by the application can improve the results.

evidence.title: Assessing the readability of AI-generated medication counseling for common Medicaid drug classes: metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin

evidence.title: Readability of dermatology patient education materials: a comparative analysis of Turkish Dermatology Association brochures and texts generated by ChatGPT and Gemini
evidence.outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient education text versus original brochures, default and low-literacy prompted
evidence.effect: All AI groups scored higher than TDA (59.08): ChatGPT 62.66, prompted ChatGPT 68.31, Gemini 66.63, prompted Gemini 68.98 (all p<0.05; r 0.242-0.753). No expert review of accuracy.
evidence.quote: Pairwise comparisons confirmed that all AI-generated texts, regardless of the specific model or prompting strategy employed, scored significantly higher than the standard TDA brochures: TDA versus ChatGPT (p = 0.047; r = 0.242), TDA versus prompted ChatGPT (p < 0.001; r = 0.667), TDA versus Gemini (p < 0.001; r = 0.548), and TDA versus prompted Gemini (p < 0.001; r = 0.753).
evidence.sample_unit: TDA brochures (each with AI-generated counterparts across four conditions)

evidence.title: Large Language Models for Clinical Note Simplification: A Systematic Review and Experimental Evaluation of Medical Text Readability
evidence.venue: Studies in health technology and informatics
evidence.outcome: Readability and technical term density of LLM-simplified German clinical notes versus originals
evidence.effect: All 10 LLMs increased text length and reduced technical term and abbreviation density, but no model achieved consistent improvements across all readability indices (Flesch, Wiener Sachtextformel, LIX, SMOG, Coleman-Liau).
evidence.quote: However, no model achieved consistent improvements across all readability indices, highlighting limitations of traditional metrics in the medical domain.

evidence.title: Performance of popular large language models in glaucoma patient education: A randomized controlled study
evidence.venue: Advances in ophthalmology practice and research
evidence.outcome: Recommended reading age and reading difficulty of LLM glaucoma education answers
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4.0 had higher recommended reading age and reading difficulty scores than the other models; the abstract gives no numbers. Baichuan 2 and ChatGPT-4.0 were rated best overall.
evidence.quote: In the first stage, Baichuan 2 and ChatGPT-4.0 outperformed the other two models, though ChatGPT-4.0 had higher recommended reading age and reading difficulty scores.

evidence.title: Chatbot Use by Patients Seeking Urogynecologic Consultation: A Randomized Trial
evidence.outcome: Readability of chatbot responses to patients
evidence.effect: Chatbot responses averaged an 11th-12th grade reading level.
evidence.quote: Chatbot responses averaged an 11th-12th grade reading level.

evidence.title: Poetic or Prosaic? Evaluating the Linguistic Quality of AI-Generated Draft Replies to Patient Portal Messages
evidence.outcome: Flesch Reading Ease of AI drafts vs final physician-sent messages
evidence.effect: Final physician messages were longer and more readable than GPT drafts; authors cite readability challenges.
evidence.quote: Final messages were longer and more readable.

evidence.title: Patient friendly summaries of oncology consultations generated by large language models - A pilot study of patient and provider satisfaction
evidence.outcome: Patient and provider ratings of clarity of LLM patient-friendly consultation summaries
evidence.effect: Patients agreed on clarity 100%; providers agreed on clarity 91%. Some summaries retained jargon; prompt to be optimized.
evidence.quote: Some of the summaries retained jargon and results from this study will be used to optimize the prompt for an expanded study.

evidence.title: Patient and Clinician Perceptions of a "People-Like-Me" Tool for Personalized Rehabilitation After Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Qualitative Interview Study
evidence.outcome: Patient comprehension of the tool's outputs (percentiles, line graphs, jargon)
evidence.effect: Most patients understood the tool's take-home message, but some patients and clinicians felt percentiles, line graphs, and medical jargon decreased clarity and comprehension.
evidence.quote: some patients and clinicians felt the use of percentiles, line graphs, and medical jargon decreased patients' clarity and comprehension of the tool

evidence.title: Patient-facing chatbots: Enhancing healthcare accessibility while navigating digital literacy challenges and isolation risks-a mixed-methods study
evidence.outcome: Patient-reported ability to understand chatbot responses and feeling understood by chatbot
evidence.effect: 213/609 (35.0%) felt they could not understand the chatbot completely; 376/614 (61.2%) felt the chatbot did not completely understand them.
evidence.quote: In surveys, 213/609 (35.0%) felt they could not understand the chatbot completely, and 376/614 (61.2%) felt the chatbot did not completely understand them.

evidence.title: Readability of Chatbot Responses in Prostate Cancer and Urological Care: Objective Metrics Versus Patient Perceptions
evidence.outcome: Objective readability of chatbot responses (FRE, LIX, WSF) versus recommended health literacy levels
evidence.effect: Responses were difficult to read (FRE 43.1 ± 9.1; LIX 52.8 ± 6.2; WSF 11.2 ± 1.6), exceeding recommendations, though 83-90% of patients perceived them as clear.
evidence.quote: Chatbot responses were objectively written at a difficult reading level, exceeding recommendations for optimized health literacy.

evidence.title: Readability of AI-Generated Patient Visit Summaries in Orthopedic Surgery: Retrospective Analysis
evidence.outcome: Proportion of AI-generated visit summaries meeting sixth- and eighth-grade readability benchmarks
evidence.effect: Mean FKGL 9.3; only 0.4% (4/982) met sixth-grade and 14.2% (139/982) met eighth-grade threshold.
evidence.quote: Only 0.4% (4/982) of PVS met the sixth-grade benchmark and 14.2% (139/982) met the eighth-grade threshold.

evidence.title: The Biased Oracle: Assessing LLMs' Understandability and Empathy in Medical Diagnoses
evidence.outcome: Readability of LLM diagnostic explanations for patients
evidence.effect: LLMs generated overly complex content as measured by readability metrics, leading to uneven accessibility; no numbers given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: However, they also generate overly complex content and display biased affective empathy, leading to uneven accessibility and support.

evidence.title: Can "AI" Be a Doctor? A Study of Empathy, Readability, and Alignment in Clinical LLMs
evidence.outcome: Readability (FKGL) of LLM responses versus physician-authored responses
evidence.effect: Larger models (GPT-5, Claude) reached FKGL up to 16.91-17.60 versus 11.47-12.50 for physician responses. Empathy prompting lowered FKGL by up to 6.87 points for GPT-5.
evidence.quote: Baseline models amplify affective polarity relative to physicians (Very Negative: 43.14-45.10% vs. 37.25%) and, in larger architectures such as GPT-5 and Claude, produce substantially higher linguistic complexity (FKGL up to 16.91-17.60 vs. 11.47-12.50 in physician-authored responses).

evidence.title: GPT-4 Enhances Readability of Online Patient Materials for Cardiac Amyloidosis
evidence.outcome: Readability of GPT-4 revised patient education materials versus institutional originals
evidence.effect: GPT-4 reduced median FKGL from 10.9 to 7.8 (IQR 7.0, 8.8); only 14/86 (16.3%) reached at least 6th-grade level.
evidence.quote: In comparison, GPT-4 revised PEMs reduced the median FKGL to 7.8 (seventh grade; IQR: 7.0, 8.8, p<0.001), with 14/86 (16.3%) achieving at least a 6th-grade reading level.

evidence.title: Assessment of the credibility of generative artificial intelligence large language models on nutritional guidelines for orthodontic patients
evidence.outcome: Readability of LLM nutrition guidance for orthodontic patients (Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level)
evidence.effect: BOS and AAO sources were more readable than the LLMs. ChatGPT 4.0 was the most readable LLM but was still difficult for readers.
evidence.quote: The readability of the responses from LLMs was difficult.

evidence.title: Performance of Large Language Artificial Intelligence Models on Clear Aligner Treatment: Evaluation of Accuracy and Readibility in Answering Questions for Patients
evidence.outcome: Readability (FKGL, FRES) of ChatGPT 4o answers to patient clear aligner questions
evidence.effect: Highest FKGL 14.53 ± 8.88 (usage questions). For the top 10 questions, mean FKGL was 13.37 ± 4.37 and mean FRES was 47.18 ± 23.69, i.e., difficult, college-level text.
evidence.quote: For the top 10 questions, the average FKGL was 13.37 ± 4.37, and the average FRES was 47.18 ± 23.69.

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT Responses to Frequently Asked Questions on Total Knee Arthroplasty
evidence.outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level) of ChatGPT-3.5 answers to patient questions about total knee arthroplasty
evidence.effect: FKGL readability scores were high, meaning responses require a high level of education; the abstract reports no numeric FKGL values and says this level can be reduced.
evidence.quote: The readability scores for FKGL were high.

evidence.title: Evaluation of Large Language Model-Generated Patient Information for Communicating Radiation Risk
evidence.outcome: Professional ratings of readability, language suitability and tone of LLM-generated radiation risk patient information
evidence.effect: Professional groups differed significantly in scoring readability, language suitability and tone, especially for higher-risk procedures; qualitative feedback showed variable balance of technical accuracy and accessible language.
evidence.quote: Significant differences were identified among professional groups in their scoring of readability, language suitability, and tone, particularly for higher-risk procedures.
evidence.sample_unit: healthcare professionals rating LLM-generated patient information

evidence.title: LLMs and Stargardt’s Disease
evidence.outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid grade level) of LLM responses to a simulated 14-year-old patient
evidence.effect: Flesch-Kincaid scores ranged 5.4-10.8, described as suitable for high school to college level; some outputs are above a typical 14-year-old's reading level.
evidence.quote: Flesch-Kincaid scores indicated a readability level suitable for high school to college (5.4-10.8).
evidence.sample_unit: LLM responses (4 models x 2 gender prompts)

evidence.title: Feeding Intelligence: Comparative Evaluation of ChatGPT and Clinical Guidelines for Nutritional Management in Head and Neck Cancer
evidence.outcome: Readability (Flesch–Kincaid grade) of ChatGPT outputs versus guidelines
evidence.effect: ChatGPT Flesch–Kincaid grade 12.9–14.2 versus guidelines 17.9–20.5; clarity 4.5 vs 3.2. ChatGPT is more readable than guidelines but still at a high grade level.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT exhibited superior patient-centered performance in clarity (4.5 vs 3.2) and self-management guidance (4.6 vs 3.0) and demonstrated more concise, readable content (Flesch–Kincaid grade 12.9–14.2) compared with guidelines (17.9–20.5).
evidence.sample_unit: nutrition-related clinical issues (ChatGPT responses compared with guidelines; 5 expert raters)

evidence.title: Evaluation of ChatGPT-5 Responses in Obstetric and Gynecological Emergencies: Concordance, Readability, and Clinical Reliability
evidence.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT-5 responses (FRES, FKGL, SMOG, CLI)
evidence.effect: FRES 40.5 ± 2.5; FKGL 11.6 ± 1.2; SMOG 10.9 ± 0.8; CLI 10.9 ± 0.8, indicating moderately technical language.
evidence.quote: Readability analyses showed that responses contained a moderate amount of technical language (FRES score = 40.5 ± 2.5; FKGL score = 11.6 ± 1.2; SMOG score = 10.9 ± 0.8; and CLI score = 10.9 ± 0.8).

evidence.title: Readability Optimization of Layperson Summaries in Urological Oncology Clinical Trials: Outcomes from the BRIDGE-AI 8 Study
evidence.outcome: Readability and content completeness of GAI-generated layperson trial summaries
evidence.effect: GAI summaries had mean FRES 73.3 ± 3.5 (middle-school level), simpler syntax and reduced lexical complexity, and 100% inclusion of guideline-defined content elements.
evidence.quote: These findings suggest that GAI tools such as Pub2Post can generate patient-facing summaries that are both accessible and comprehensive.

evidence.title: The Promise and Peril of Large Language Models in Digital Health: GPT-4 Personalizes Cardiovascular Patient Education but Amplifies Gender Biases
evidence.outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Reading Ease) of GPT-4 revised patient education materials
evidence.effect: Readability was maintained after GPT-4 revision; the gender-inclusivity checklist median rose from 3.0/10 (original) to 8.0 (male-tailored) and 10.0 (female-tailored).
evidence.quote: Readability was maintained.

evidence.title: A Comparative Analysis of Five AI Chatbots in Providing Patient Education on Smile Design
evidence.outcome: Readability (FRE, FKGL) of chatbot patient-education responses versus recommended patient reading level
evidence.effect: Readability differed significantly across chatbots (FRE p=0.004; FKGL p<0.001); ChatGPT-5 required the highest reading level; most responses were above eighth-grade level.
evidence.quote: Most chatbot responses were above an eighth-grade reading level, which may challenge general patient comprehension.

evidence.title: Comparative efficacy of ChatGPT-5.1 Auto and DeepSeek-V3.1 Thinking in answering patients’ questions on cervical spine surgery
evidence.outcome: Readability of LLM answers to cervical spine surgery patient questions (FKGL, FRES)
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-5.1 Auto FKGL 10.60 and FRES 39.50; DeepSeek-V3.1 Thinking FKGL 7.80 and FRES 61.70 (P<0.001). DeepSeek text was easier to read, and ChatGPT text was harder to read.
evidence.quote: While ChatGPT-5.1 Auto excelled in completeness, DeepSeek-V3.1 Thinking demonstrated superior readability.

evidence.title: Comparative Readability of Large Language Models Responses to Male Infertility Questions: Impact of Contextual Prompting
evidence.outcome: Readability (FRE, SMOG) of LLM responses to male infertility FAQs without context
evidence.effect: Unprompted, DeepSeek was most readable (FRE 46.28±6.86; SMOG 11.71±0.76); Claude least readable (FRE 23.83±12.29; SMOG 16.37±2.47), i.e., difficult, college-level text.
evidence.quote: In the non-prompted condition, DeepSeek generated the most readable responses (mean FRE 46.28±6.86; mean SMOG 11.71±0.76), whereas Claude produced the least readable outputs (mean FRE 23.83±12.29; mean SMOG 16.37±2.47).
evidence.sample_unit: FAQs on male infertility submitted to each of five LLMs under two prompting conditions

evidence.title: Large Language Models as Ophthalmic Patient Educators: A Comparative Evaluation of Readability, Understandability, and Actionability
evidence.outcome: Readability (Flesch Reading Ease) of LLM ophthalmic patient education responses
evidence.effect: Median Flesch Reading Ease was 33.6 for Perplexity, 41.3 for ChatGPT, and 43.6 for Gemini; Perplexity differed from ChatGPT (Holm-adjusted P = .003), Gemini did not (P = .42).
evidence.quote: Median Flesch Reading Ease differed between Perplexity and ChatGPT (33.6 vs 41.3; Holm-adjusted P = .003), while Gemini did not differ from ChatGPT (43.6 vs 41.3; Holm-adjusted P = .42).

evidence.title: Evaluating 11 Large Language Models in Answering Key Questions on Ovarian Cancer
evidence.outcome: Clinician-rated ease of understanding of LLM answers to ovarian cancer FAQs (5-point Likert)
evidence.effect: Claude 3 Opus averaged 4.38, Mistral Large 4.36 and GPT-4o 4.33 for ease of understanding; readability was rated by surgical fellows, not by patients.
evidence.quote: Claude 3 Opus produced the easiest-to-understand answers (average score 4.38), followed by Mistral Large (4.36) and GPT-4o (4.33).
evidence.sample_unit: questions (FAQs), each answered by 11 LLMs and rated by 3 fellows

evidence.title: Readability, Quality, Understandability, and Actionability of ChatGPT Generated GI Patient Education vs AGA Patient Center
evidence.outcome: Readability, understandability, and actionability of ChatGPT patient education versus AGA materials
evidence.effect: ChatGPT text was at a higher reading level (FKGL 10.33 vs 8.72), while PEMAT understandability (87.91% vs 86.52%) and actionability (78.57% vs 77.93%) did not differ significantly.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-generated gastrointestinal patient education demonstrated similar quality, understandability, and actionability compared with professional society materials but was written at a significantly higher reading level.

evidence.title: Expert evaluation and readability of conversational AI responses to common ophthalmic patient questions: an exploratory generational cross-sectional study
evidence.outcome: Readability of AI patient responses (Flesch–Szigriszt Index, INFLESZ category)
evidence.effect: Mean FSI 67.7 vs 53.9 in earlier data, a shift from 'somewhat difficult' to 'fairly easy'. Readability had minimal correlation with expert-rated quality.
evidence.quote: In contrast, readability showed a substantial increase (mean FSI 67.7 vs 53.9), corresponding to a shift from “somewhat difficult” to “fairly easy” patient comprehension.

evidence.title: Enhancing health literacy for people with cystic fibrosis (CF): Quality and readability of microbiology information generated by artificial intelligence (AI) platforms - A cross sectional infodemiology study
evidence.outcome: Readability (FRES, FKGL) of AI answers to cystic fibrosis patient questions
evidence.effect: Microbiology answers: mean FRES 34.30 (Gemini), 25.72 (AI Overview), 19.46 (ChatGPT 4.0); FKGL 11.54, 12.74, 15.10. General CF answers: FKGL 9.52, 9.66, 12.98. Readability did not meet target standards.
evidence.quote: The readability, however, did not meet the target reference standards and further research is required to ascertain if readability can be improved by using simplification and detailed sentence commands.
evidence.sample_unit: questions (25 microbiology, 25 general CF), each answered by three AI platforms

evidence.title: Evaluation of the Quality and Reliability of ChatGPT-4's Responses on Allergen Immunotherapy Using Validated Tools
evidence.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT-4 answers on allergen immunotherapy (Flesch Reading Ease and Grade Level)
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4 answers required a college graduate level of education and were very difficult to read.
evidence.quote: Finally, ChatGPT-4 answers required a “college graduate” level of education to be understood as they were very difficult to read.

evidence.title: ChatGPT 3.5 and 4.0: A Head to Head Comparison in Generating Pharyngitis Patient Guides
evidence.outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, Flesch Reading Ease) of ChatGPT pharyngitis patient answers
evidence.effect: Both ChatGPT-3.5 and ChatGPT-4.0 required a high educational level; ChatGPT-4.0 was marginally more readable (p < 0.05).
evidence.quote: Readability scores indicated both versions required a high educational level, with ChatGPT-4.0 showing marginally better readability (p < 0.05).

evidence.title: AI-based chatbots and orthodontic retention: A comparative analysis of response quality and readability
evidence.outcome: Readability (FRE, FKGL) of chatbot orthodontic retention responses versus recommended patient education thresholds
evidence.effect: FRE indicated difficult readability; FKGL corresponded to high school- to college-level reading grade; no difference among chatbots (p > 0.05).
evidence.quote: However, all responses were written at a readability level exceeding recommended thresholds for patient education materials, which may limit their practical usefulness.

evidence.title: Assessment of ChatGPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Pro Responses to Frequently Asked Patient Questions in Oral Surgery: A Study on Validity, Readability, and Temporal Consistency
evidence.outcome: Readability of chatbot responses (Ateşman score, higher is easier) for patient questions
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-5 scored 83.43 vs Gemini 2.5 Pro 71.86 (p < 0.001), so ChatGPT-5 responses were significantly more readable.
evidence.quote: Readability analysis demonstrated that ChatGPT-5 produced significantly more readable responses than Gemini 2.5 Pro 2.5 Pro, with higher Ateşman readability scores (83.43 vs. 71.86, p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Evaluating Cross-Platform Large Language Models for Patient Education in Hypertension and Chronic Kidney Disease: Quality, Readability, and Actionability
evidence.outcome: Comprehensibility (readability, understandability, actionability) of LLM patient education outputs
evidence.effect: Median PEMAT-P understandability 69.20 but actionability 20.00; high reading burden (FRES 20.53, SMOG 16.36).
evidence.quote: Under standardized English prompts, large language model-generated patient education texts for hypertension with chronic kidney disease showed relatively good understandability but limited actionability and source transparency, while overall reading burden remained high.

evidence.title: Divergence Between Clinical Accuracy and Readability in Large Language Models: A Comparative Study in Hypogonadism
evidence.outcome: Readability of LLM responses (ARI, FRES, GFI) for hypogonadism patient questions
evidence.effect: Gemini produced significantly more readable responses (lower ARI and GFI, higher FRES) than ChatGPT and Claude (all p < 0.001); Claude was most accurate but less readable.
evidence.quote: Gemini generated significantly more readable responses, characterized by lower ARI and GFI values and higher FRES scores compared with ChatGPT and Claude (all p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Can Large Language Models Provide High-Quality Information for Patients with Multidrug-Resistant Organism Infections: A Multidimensional Comparative Analysis of DeepSeek-V3, ChatGPT-5.2, Gemini-3, and Grok-4
evidence.outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of LLM patient education outputs via readability indices
evidence.effect: All model outputs exceeded the sixth-grade reading level recommended for patient materials (Flesch–Kincaid, Gunning Fog, Flesch Reading Ease).
evidence.quote: Readability analyses revealed that all model outputs surpassed the American Medical Association's recommended sixth-grade reading level for patient materials.

evidence.title: Evaluation of Large Language Models for Post-Cystectomy Sexual Health Counseling in Women
evidence.outcome: Readability of LLM-generated sexual health information versus recommended reading levels
evidence.effect: All three models produced content above recommended reading levels; PCA showed one dominant component explaining 76.7% of variance across readability indices.
evidence.quote: All models produced content that exceeded recommended reading levels.
evidence.sample_unit: clinical questions (each in long-form and short-form, across 3 LLMs)

evidence.title: Assessing the Quality, Safety, and Readability of Large Language Model Responses from ChatGPT and Gemini for Knee Osteoarthritis Patient Education
evidence.outcome: Readability grade level of chatbot knee osteoarthritis patient-education responses versus recommended 6th-8th grade level
evidence.effect: Both platforms exceeded the recommended level; Fry score was 11.90 ± 1.52 for ChatGPT vs 10.70 ± 1.62 for Gemini (p = 0.003).
evidence.quote: ChatGPT produced higher Fry Readability Formula scores (11.90 ± 1.52 vs 10.70 ± 1.62; p = 0.003), the only readability difference to survive correction; both platforms produced text well above the recommended sixth-to-eighth-grade reading level for patient education.

evidence.title: Reliability and Clinical Accuracy of ChatGPT in Post-FESS Counselling: A Multi-Reviewer Evaluation
evidence.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT postoperative counselling responses (Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level)
evidence.effect: Mean FRE 41.2 and FKGL 12.8, indicating content written at a senior-school to college reading level.
evidence.quote: Readability analysis revealed a mean FRE score of 41.2 and an FKGL of 12.8, indicating content written at a senior-school to college reading level.

evidence.title: High Overall Performance but Limited Multidisciplinary Depth: A Cross- Sectional Evaluation of ChatGPT in Pathological Fractures of Plasma Cell Tumors
evidence.outcome: Readability grade level and patient comprehensibility rating of ChatGPT answers on pathological fractures
evidence.effect: Readability corresponded to about 10th-12th grade. Patient comprehensibility received the highest expert ratings among the five domains.
evidence.quote: The readability level corresponded to approximately 10th–12th grade.

evidence.title: Assessing the Quality of AI-Generated Health Information: A Comparative Study of Large Language Models in Patient Education on Dental Veneers
evidence.outcome: Flesch Reading Ease of chatbot answers to dental veneer patient questions
evidence.effect: Mean FRES was 38.92 ± 9.26 for Gemini-3.5 Flash (highest) and 25.33 ± 11.67 for DeepSeek-V4 (lowest). Both are in the difficult-to-read range, so no chatbot produced plain-language answers.
evidence.quote: For readability, Gemini-3.5 Flash (38.92 ± 9.26 ) obtained the highest FRES score, while DeepSeek-V4 (25.33 ± 11.67) showed the lowest readability.

evidence.title: Quality of Olfactory Dysfunction Information Across Digital Health Platforms: A Comparative Study of Google Search and Artificial Intelligence Platforms
evidence.outcome: Readability (FKGL, SMOG) of OD information versus NHS recommended grade 6-8
evidence.effect: Mean FKGL 11.01 exceeded NHS recommendations (Grades 6–8); only 27.7% of sources met the target; readability poor across all platforms.
evidence.quote: Mean readability (FKGL 11.01) exceeded NHS recommendations (Grades 6–8), with only 27.7% of sources meeting the target.
evidence.sample_unit: standardised search terms applied across five platforms

evidence.title: Evaluating Five Generative AI Chatbots for Myocarditis-Related Public Health Consultation: A Multidimensional Assessment of Safety, Accuracy, Empathy, Reliability, Quality, and Readability
evidence.outcome: Readability of chatbot responses against sixth-grade target for patient-facing information
evidence.effect: No model met the prespecified sixth-grade readability target; significant between-model differences on all readability indices (all P<0.001).
evidence.quote: No model met the prespecified sixth-grade readability target for patient-facing information.

evidence.title: The Illusion of Understanding: A Randomized Controlled Trial of LLM-Generated Lay Summaries of Brain MRI Reports
evidence.outcome: objective comprehension of findings with AI lay summary
evidence.effect: 58.3% intervention vs 59.4% control (OR 0.97, 95% CI: 0.90–1.06, P = .54)
evidence.quote: Adding an LLM-generated lay summary to brain MRI reports did not improve the rate of correct identification of symptom-explaining findings (58.3% vs 59.4%; odds ratio, 0.97; 95%CI: 0.90–1.06; P = .54).

evidence.title: Large Language Models for Pulmonary Embolism Health Education: A Four- Model Comparison of Reliability, Quality, and Readability
evidence.outcome: Readability of LLM pulmonary embolism education responses versus sixth-grade benchmarks
evidence.effect: No model met sixth-grade readability standards; median grade-level indices ranged from approximately 9 to 16; median FRES 34.80 to 47.90.
evidence.quote: No model met sixth-grade readability standards.

evidence.title: GPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3 responses to common migraine questions: a cross-sectional comparative study of accuracy, completeness, empathy, readability and safety
evidence.outcome: Readability (Ateşman score) of LLM answers to patient-facing migraine questions
evidence.effect: Ateşman readability was 74.75 ± 17.43 for DeepSeek-V3 vs 60.70 ± 19.97 for GPT-4o (adjusted p < 0.001); GPT-4o answers were harder to read.
evidence.quote: DeepSeek-V3 had higher accuracy scores than GPT-4o (4.54 ± 0.49 vs 4.37 ± 0.50; Holm-adjusted p = 0.026), higher completeness scores (3.98 ± 0.44 vs 3.46 ± 0.61; adjusted p < 0.001), and higher Ateşman readability scores (74.75 ± 17.43 vs 60.70 ± 19.97; adjusted p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Evaluating General-Purpose versus Medical-Specific Large Language Models for Perioperative Deep Vein Thrombosis Consultation: Perspectives from Physicians, Nurses, and Patients
evidence.outcome: Readability level of LLM DVT consultation responses using Chinese Readability Platform
evidence.effect: One medical-specific model required senior high school level; the other three required only junior high school level.
evidence.quote: Readability varied substantially: one medical-specific model required senior high school level, whereas the other three required only junior high school level.
evidence.sample_unit: evaluators (5 physicians, 5 nurses, 5 patients) rating responses to 9 questions from 4 LLMs

evidence.title: Large Language Models for Carotid-Cavernous Fistula Patient Education: A Multidimensional Comparative Study
evidence.outcome: Readability of LLM patient education responses (six readability indices) across models
evidence.effect: All six readability metrics differed significantly among models; Doubao produced more linguistically complex responses. Excessive complexity may limit suitability for public-facing education. PEMAT understandability did not differ (P = 0.063).
evidence.quote: All six readability metrics differed significantly among models, with Doubao generally producing more linguistically complex responses.

evidence.title: Evaluating AI Chatbots as Patient Education Tools for Dental Trauma: A Cross-Sectional Comparison of Information Quality and Readability
evidence.outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of AI-generated patient education content
evidence.effect: No model met the sixth-grade readability standard; median Flesch Reading Ease 40.98 to 51.53 versus target ≥ 80.
evidence.quote: Moreover, none met the prespecified sixth-grade readability standard: median grade-level index values were ≥ 6 and median Flesch Reading Ease Scores ranged from 40.98 to 51.53, below the target of ≥ 80.

evidence.title: Evaluation of Vertigo-Related Information from Artificial Intelligence Chatbot
evidence.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT-4o vertigo responses (Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level)
evidence.effect: Readability analysis showed higher difficulty in diagnostic texts; readability judged to need improvement. No numeric readability scores reported in the abstract.
evidence.quote: Readability analysis revealed higher difficulty in diagnostic texts.

evidence.title: Responses of AI Chatbots to Testosterone Replacement Therapy: Patient's Beware!
evidence.outcome: Readability (FRES, FKGL) of chatbot testosterone replacement therapy answers for patients
evidence.effect: Even the most readable chatbot, Perplexity AI, produced text at about an eleventh-grade level. ChatGPT and Perplexity differed significantly on FRES and FKGL.
evidence.quote: Despite Perplexity scoring higher in readability, the generated text still maintained an eleventh-grade complexity.

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence-based chatbots in providing space maintainer related information for pediatric patients and parents: A comparative study
evidence.outcome: Readability of chatbot answers on pediatric space maintainers (FRES, FKRGL)
evidence.effect: Readability scores for both ChatGPT-3.5 and ChatGPT-4 required college-degree education, above typical patient/parent reading levels.
evidence.quote: The readability scores seemed to require an education of a college degree and the similarity levels were lesser than 10% for both chatbots whit a high originality.

evidence.title: Assessing the Clinical Support Capabilities of ChatGPT-4o and ChatGPT-4o Mini in Managing Lumbar Disc Herniation
evidence.outcome: Readability of LLM-generated responses measured by Flesch Reading Ease
evidence.effect: Flesch Reading Ease scores for both ChatGPT-4.0 and ChatGPT-4.0-mini rated content 'very difficult to read', potentially limiting patient accessibility.
evidence.quote: The Flesch Reading Ease scores for both models indicated that their generated content was “very difficult to read,” potentially limiting patient accessibility.

evidence.title: A Comparison of Quality and Readability of ChatGPT-4 generated and Human-generated Patient Education Materials for Total Knee Arthroplasty
evidence.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT-4 TKA patient education materials versus human-generated materials

evidence.title: Bridging the Gap Between Urological Research and Patient Understanding: The Role of Large Language Models in Automated Generation of Layperson's Summaries
