evidence.quote: However, AI-generated responses were more likely to be classified at an advanced reading level, while UCF responses showed improved readability (college or higher reading level: ChatGPT = 100%, Bard = 66%, and UCF = 19%), p < 0.001.

evidence.title: Dr. Google to Dr. ChatGPT: assessing the content and quality of artificial intelligence-generated medical information on appendicitis
evidence.outcome: Readability (FKGL, FRE) of chatbot-generated appendicitis information versus public reading level
evidence.effect: FKGL and FRE were 14.6/23.8 (ChatGPT-3.5), 11.9/33.9 (ChatGPT-4), 8.6/52.8 (Bard), 11.0/36.6 (Claude-2), indicating college-level difficulty.
evidence.quote: Regarding readability, FKGL and FRE scores of ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4, Bard, and Claude-2 were 14.6 and 23.8, 11.9 and 33.9, 8.6 and 52.8, 11.0 and 36.6, respectively, indicating difficulty readability at a college reading skill level.
evidence.sample_unit: chatbot-generated texts on appendicitis (one per chatbot)

evidence.title: Generative Pre-trained Transformer 4 makes cardiovascular magnetic resonance reports easy to understand
evidence.venue: Journal of cardiovascular magnetic resonance : official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance
evidence.outcome: Readability (ARI) and layperson understandability of GPT-4 simplified reports vs original reports
evidence.effect: ARI 10 [9-12] original vs 5 [4-6] GPT-4 (p<0.001); 2/60 (3%) GPT-4 reports vs 18/20 (90%) originals at 8th grade level or higher; laypersons rated GPT-4 easier to understand (1 vs 4, p<0.001).
evidence.quote: Eighteen out of 20 (90%) standard CMR reports and 2/60 (3%) GPT-generated reports had an ARI score corresponding to the 8th grade level or higher.
evidence.sample_unit: GPT-4 generated simplified CMR reports (from 20 original reports)

evidence.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence to Transform Inpatient Discharge Summaries to Patient-Friendly Language and Format
evidence.outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level) of original discharge summaries versus LLM patient-friendly versions
evidence.effect: Mean FK grade level 11.0 (SD 1.5) for original summaries vs 6.2 (SD 0.5) for LLM patient-friendly versions (P < .001); PEMAT understandability 13% vs 81%.
evidence.quote: Mean (SD) Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level was significantly lower in the patient-friendly discharge summaries (6.2 [0.5] vs 11.0 [1.5]; P < .001).

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence insights into osteoporosis: assessing ChatGPT's information quality and readability
evidence.outcome: Readability (FKRE, FKGL) of ChatGPT osteoporosis responses versus patient-comprehensible level
evidence.effect: FKRE mean 28.71 (range 13.71-56.06); FKGL mean 13.25 (range 8.48-17.63); abstract states about 17 years of education needed. EQIP mean 48.71, 'serious problems with quality'.
evidence.quote: The FKRE scores spanned from 13.71 to 56.06 with a mean value of 28.71 and the FKGL varied between 8.48 and 17.63, with a mean value of 13.25.

evidence.title: Generative artificial intelligence chatbots may provide appropriate informational responses to common vascular surgery questions by patients
evidence.outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient education responses versus plain-language comprehension
evidence.effect: ChatGPT responses readable only at post-secondary level (FRE 29.4, FKGL 14.5); Bard at high-school level (FRE 58.9, FKGL 8.2).
evidence.quote: Bard's mean readability scores were 58.9 ± 10.5, 8.2 ± 1.7, and 11.0 ± 2.0, respectively, indicating that responses were readable with a high-school education (p < .0001 for three metrics).

evidence.title: Dr. Google vs. Dr. ChatGPT: Exploring the Use of Artificial Intelligence in Ophthalmology by Comparing the Accuracy, Safety, and Readability of Responses to Frequently Asked Patient Questions Regarding Cataracts and Cataract Surgery
evidence.outcome: Readability grade level of ChatGPT responses to cataract FAQs versus Google
evidence.effect: ChatGPT responses were significantly longer and written at a higher reading level than Google (p < .001), with average grade level 14.8 (college level).
evidence.quote: Responses to 20 patient FAQs generated by ChatGPT were significantly longer and written at a higher reading level than responses provided by Google (p < .001), with an average grade level of 14.8 (college level).

evidence.title: The Emerging Role of AI in Patient Education: A Comparative Analysis of the Accuracy of Large Language Models for Pelvic Organ Prolapse
evidence.venue: Medical principles and practice : international journal of the Kuwait University, Health Science Centre
evidence.outcome: Readability (SMOG, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level) of LLM patient education answers versus RCOG originals
evidence.effect: ChatGPT answers were harder to read than BARD, Bing, and the original RCOG answers; no numeric grade levels are given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: In terms of readability, ChatGPT exhibited higher difficulty than BARD, Bing, and the original RCOG answers.

evidence.title: The quality and readability of patient information provided by ChatGPT: can AI reliably explain common ENT operations?
evidence.venue: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
evidence.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT patient information (FRES) before and after simplification
evidence.effect: ChatGPT readability was poor, with mean FRES of 38.9 and 55.1 pre- and post-simplification, respectively; ENT UK leaflets were consistently more readable.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT readability was poor, with mean FRES of 38.9 and 55.1 pre- and post-simplification, respectively.
evidence.sample_unit: ChatGPT responses to standard and simplified questions on three ENT operations

evidence.title: Chat Generative Pretraining Transformer Answers Patient-focused Questions in Cervical Spine Surgery
evidence.outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of ChatGPT patient education responses
evidence.effect: Readability at 13.5 grade level originally, 11.2 after rephrasing prompt; readability score 1.2/2 for layperson.
evidence.quote: Readability was determined to be at the 13.5 grade level originally and at the 11.2 grade level after prompting.

evidence.title: Quality of Large Language Model Responses to Radiation Oncology Patient Care Questions
evidence.outcome: Readability grade level of LLM answers versus expert answers to patient questions
evidence.effect: Mean (SD) readability consensus score was 10.63 (3.17) for expert answers vs 13.64 (2.22) for LLM answers (P < .001), indicating 10th grade and college reading levels, respectively.
evidence.quote: The mean (SD) readability consensus score for expert answers was 10.63 (3.17) vs 13.64 (2.22) for LLM answers (P < .001), indicating 10th grade and college reading levels, respectively.

evidence.title: Responses of Five Different Artificial Intelligence Chatbots to the Top Searched Queries About Erectile Dysfunction: A Comparative Analysis
evidence.outcome: Readability of chatbot responses (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level and Reading Ease) to erectile dysfunction queries
evidence.effect: None of the five chatbots reached the necessary readability level; Bard was the most readable (higher FKRE and FKGL, p = 0.001), and Copilot had the best EQIP and DISCERN quality ratings (p = 0.001).
evidence.quote: None of the AI chatbots achieved the necessary degree of readability.
evidence.sample_unit: queries (top searched erectile dysfunction terms, each given to five chatbots)

evidence.title: A Multidisciplinary Assessment of ChatGPT's Knowledge of Amyloidosis: Observational Study
evidence.outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of AI-generated patient education responses
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4 responses averaged grade 15.5 (SD 1.9), well above the AMA-recommended fifth- to sixth-grade reading level.
evidence.quote: However, ChatGPT's responses exceeded the American Medical Association's recommended fifth- to sixth-grade reading level.

evidence.title: Performance of Artificial Intelligence Chatbots on Glaucoma Questions Adapted From Patient Brochures
evidence.outcome: Readability of chatbot patient-education responses relative to patient comprehension levels
evidence.effect: ChatGPT and Bing responses were at FKGL 13.01 and 11.73, above AAO brochures at 8.11; Bard was 7.90.
evidence.quote: With accuracy scores and comprehensiveness below that of AAO brochures and elevated readability levels, AI chatbots require improvements to be a more useful supplementary source of glaucoma information for patients.

evidence.title: Evaluation of Patient Education Materials From Large-Language Artificial Intelligence Models on Carpal Tunnel Release
evidence.outcome: Readability and grade level of ChatGPT versus Google answers to carpal tunnel release FAQs
evidence.effect: ChatGPT answers were significantly longer and statistically significantly more difficult to read, at a higher grade level, than Google's answers across multiple readability algorithms.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT's answers were significantly longer than Google's and multiple readability analysis algorithms found ChatGPT responses to be statistically significantly more difficult to read and at a higher grade level than Google's.
evidence.sample_unit: Google FAQs on carpal tunnel release with paired ChatGPT answers

evidence.title: The Performance of Chatbots and the AAPOS Website as a Tool for Amblyopia Education

evidence.effect: PEMAT-U: website 81.5%, Bard 77.6%, ChatGPT-3.5 76.1%, Bing Chat 71.5% (P<.05); PEMAT-A: website 74.6%, Bard 69.2%, ChatGPT-3.5 67.8%, Bing Chat 64.8% (P<.05).
evidence.quote: The AAPOS website and chatbots, especially Chat-GPT, provided difficult-to-read data for patient education regarding amblyopia.

evidence.title: Quantitative Comparison of Chatbots on Common Rhinology Pathologies
evidence.outcome: Flesch Reading Ease readability of chatbot responses on rhinology treatments
evidence.effect: FRE scores were 33.17 (ChatGPT), 35.93 (Plus), 46.50 (Bard), 46.32 (Bing); Bard and Bing were more readable than ChatGPT and Plus, but all scores are in the difficult range.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT, Plus, Bard, and Bing had FRE readability scores of 33.17, 35.93, 46.50, and 46.32, respectively, indicating higher readability for Bard and Bing compared to ChatGPT (p = 0.003, p = 0.008) and Plus (p = 0.025, p = 0.048).

evidence.title: Walking forward or on hold: Could the ChatGPT be applied for seeking health information in neurosurgical settings?
evidence.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT 3.5 vs 4.0 responses (word count, Flesch-Kincaid reading ease and grade level)
evidence.effect: Version 4.0 output was harder to read: more words, lower Flesch-Kincaid reading ease score, and higher Flesch-Kincaid grade level than 3.5. No numeric values given in the abstract.
evidence.quote: As for readability, there was a higher demand for readers to comprehend the output text in the 4.0 version (more counts of words; lower Flesch-Kincaid reading ease score; and higher Flesch-Kincaid grade level).

evidence.title: Evaluating Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer Responses to Common Pediatric In-toeing Questions
evidence.outcome: Reading grade level of ChatGPT responses versus patient-appropriate level
evidence.effect: ChatGPT responses averaged Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level 12.7 (±1.4), collegiate level, versus 4.9 (±2.1) for the questions.
evidence.quote: However, ChatGPT's responses were at a collegiate level, averaging 12.7 (±1.4).

evidence.title: How artificial intelligence can provide information about subdural hematoma: Assessment of readability, reliability, and quality of ChatGPT, BARD, and perplexity responses
evidence.outcome: Readability of chatbot responses on subdural hematoma versus recommended sixth-grade reading level
evidence.effect: Median readability scores of ChatGPT, Bard, and Perplexity differed significantly from the sixth-grade level in all formulas (P < .001); all three were difficult to read.
evidence.quote: The readability levels of the responses of artificial intelligence applications such as ChatGPT, Bard, and perplexity are significantly higher than the recommended 6th grade level.

evidence.title: How good is ChatGPT at answering patients' questions related to early detection of oral (mouth) cancer?
evidence.venue: Oral surgery, oral medicine, oral pathology and oral radiology

evidence.effect: Mean FKS reading ease 38.4% ± 29.9%; mean SMOG index 11.65 ± 8.4; mean actionability 47.3% ± 18.9%.
evidence.quote: The mean FKS reading ease score was 38.4% ± 29.9%, while the mean SMOG index readability score was 11.65 ± 8.4.

evidence.title: Assessing the Responses of Large Language Models (ChatGPT-4, Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot) to Frequently Asked Questions in Breast Imaging: A Study on Readability and Accuracy
evidence.outcome: Readability (Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level) of LLM responses to breast imaging questions
evidence.effect: Gemini and Microsoft Copilot scored higher on readability scales (p < 0.001) than ChatGPT-4; ChatGPT-4 readability issues may limit its utility in patient education.
evidence.quote: While LLMs such as ChatGPT-4 show promise in providing accurate responses, readability issues may limit their utility in patient education.

evidence.title: Unlocking the future of patient Education: ChatGPT vs. LexiComp® as sources of patient education materials
evidence.venue: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
evidence.outcome: Understandability (PEMAT-P) and readability of ChatGPT patient education materials versus LexiComp
evidence.effect: PEMAT-P understandability did not differ (77.9% vs 72.5%, P=0.193), but reading grade level was higher (8.6 vs 5.6, P<0.001); fewer passive sentences and lower word count.
evidence.quote: No difference was found in the PEMAT-P understandability score of PEMs produced by ChatGPT versus LexiComp® [77.9% (11.0) vs. 72.5% (2.4), P=0.193].

evidence.title: Decoding medical jargon: The use of AI language models (ChatGPT-4, BARD, microsoft copilot) in radiology reports
evidence.outcome: Readability and understandability (PEMAT) of AI-simplified radiology reports for patients
evidence.effect: All three models simplified jargon, with BARD showing superior readability scores. All models scored above 70% on understandability, with ChatGPT-4 and BARD leading (p < 0.001, both).
evidence.quote: All three AI models successfully transformed medical jargon into more accessible language, with BARD showing superior readability scores.

evidence.title: Physician and Artificial Intelligence Chatbot Responses to Cancer Questions From Social Media
evidence.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of chatbot and physician responses to patient cancer questions
evidence.effect: Mean FK grade: physicians 10.11; chatbot 3 10.31 (P>.99); chatbot 1 12.33 (P<.001); chatbot 2 11.32 (P=.01). All above plain-language levels.
evidence.quote: The mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of physician responses (mean, 10.11 [95% CI, 9.21-11.03]) was not significantly different from chatbot 3 responses (mean, 10.31 [95% CI, 9.89-10.72]; P > .99) but was lower than those from chatbot 1 (mean, 12.33 [95% CI, 11.84-12.83]; P < .001) and chatbot 2 (mean, 11.32 [95% CI, 11.05-11.79]; P = .01).

evidence.title: Utility of Large Language Models for Health Care Professionals and Patients in Navigating Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: Comparison of the Performance of ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4, and Bard

evidence.quote: however, ChatGPT-4 showed excessively technical language, with only 10 of 22 (46%) rated as “3” in language appropriateness compared to 17 of 21 (81%) for ChatGPT-3.5.

evidence.title: Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer (ChatGPT) - 3.5 Responses Require Advanced Readability for the General Population and May Not Effectively Supplement Patient-Related Information Provided by the Treating Surgeon Regarding Common Questions About Rotator Cuff Repair

evidence.title: A quality and readability comparison of artificial intelligence and popular health website education materials for common hand surgery procedures

evidence.title: Assessment of the Quality and Readability of Information Provided by ChatGPT in Relation to the Use of Platelet-Rich Plasma Therapy for Osteoarthritis
evidence.outcome: Reading grade level of ChatGPT responses about PRP therapy versus recommended 8th grade level
evidence.effect: Mean reading grade levels of 17.18 (ChatGPT 3.5) and 16.36 (ChatGPT 4), significantly above the recommended 8th grade level for patient education materials.

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT-3.5 and ChatGPT-4.0 Responses on Hyperlipidemia for Patient Education

evidence.effect: Version 3.5 had a significantly higher grade reading level than version 4.0 (p = 0.0002). Version 4.0 was more readable but still exceeded the NIH-recommended eighth-grade level.

evidence.title: Reliability and readability analysis of ChatGPT-4 and Google Bard as a patient information source for the most commonly applied radionuclide treatments in cancer patients

evidence.title: ChatGPT and low back pain - Evaluating AI-driven patient education in the context of interventional pain medicine

evidence.title: Transforming cataract care through artificial intelligence: an evaluation of large language models' performance in addressing cataract-related queries

evidence.title: A Cross-Sectional Study Assessing the Suitability of ChatGPT and DeepSeek AI for Generating Patient Education Guides on Imaging Modalities in Stroke
evidence.outcome: Readability (grade level, ease score) of AI-generated stroke imaging patient education guides

evidence.quote: ChatGPT often produced slightly higher grade levels, while DeepSeek AI had higher ease scores for some modalities.

evidence.title: Large language models to develop evidence-based strategies for primary and secondary cardiovascular prevention

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence Versus Professional Standards: A Cross-Sectional Comparative Study of GPT, Gemini, and ENT UK in Delivering Patient Information on ENT Conditions

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT's ability to simplify scientific abstracts for clinicians and the public

evidence.title: Readability versus accuracy in LLM-transformed radiology reports: stakeholder preferences across reading grade levels

evidence.quote: Lower reading grades improved readability but increased errors, while higher grades improved accuracy but reduced readability.

evidence.title: The quality, accuracy, and readability of information about hidradenitis suppurativa provided by artificial intelligence: Comparative analysis of ChatGPT, Copilot, and Perplexity

evidence.title: Quality and Readability Analysis of Artificial Intelligence-Generated Medical Information Related to Prostate Cancer: A Cross-Sectional Study of ChatGPT and DeepSeek

evidence.title: Performance of ChatGPT-4o in Providing Information on Pediatric Inborn Errors of Immunity: A Cross-Sectional Evaluation
evidence.outcome: Plain-language readability and PEMAT understandability of ChatGPT-4o outputs
evidence.effect: High reading level (FKGL 10.83-12.96), but PEMAT understandability 71.80 ± 5.75% (professional) and 80.80 ± 4.73% (patient/caregiver), p = 0.001.
evidence.quote: Mean PEMAT understandability scores were 71.80 ± 5.75% for professional queries and 80.80 ± 4.73% for patient/caregiver queries (p = 0.001).

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence-powered chatbots for oral anticancer drug patient information: an assessment of quality
evidence.outcome: Readability of chatbot answers on oral anticancer drugs (Flesch reading-ease score)
evidence.effect: Mean Flesch reading-ease scores were 38.8 (Copilot) and 50.9 (Gemini), indicating low readability.
evidence.quote: Both chatbots' answers demonstrated low readability according to the overall mean Flesch reading-ease scores of 38.8 (Copilot) and 50.9 (Gemini).
evidence.sample_unit: chatbot answers (2 chatbots x 20 drugs x 4 questions x 3 repetitions)

evidence.title: Breast cancer patients' questions about radiotherapy-induced skin toxicity: A comparative analysis of ChatGPT-4.0 and Gemini 2.5 flash
evidence.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid readability grade level of LLM answers to patient radiotherapy questions
evidence.effect: ChatGPT aligned with an 8th-grade level, whereas Gemini operated at an 11th-grade level.
evidence.quote: Readability analysis revealed that ChatGPT aligned with an 8th-grade level, whereas Gemini operated at an 11th-grade level.

evidence.title: AI dialogues in cartilage repair: which guides evidence-based decisions better?
evidence.venue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
evidence.outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid grade level) of LLM and Google answers to cartilage repair questions
evidence.effect: Grade Level 12.6-13.2 for Google vs. 15.7-17.4 for LLMs, far above typical patient reading levels; Google's lower score attributed to snippet brevity.
evidence.quote: Readability analysis paradoxically favored Google (Grade Level 12.6-13.2 vs. 15.7-17.4 for LLMs), attributable to extreme snippet brevity inflating formulaic scores rather than genuine comprehensibility.

evidence.title: Intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy: Comparative evaluation of appropriateness and readability of large language model chatbots' responses to frequently asked patient questions
evidence.outcome: Readability of chatbot answers to anti-VEGF patient questions across five readability indices
evidence.effect: Significant differences across all readability indices (P<0.001); Gemini 3 had the highest Flesch Reading Ease, while Grok 4 produced more complex texts requiring higher educational levels.
evidence.quote: Gemini 3 achieved the highest Flesch Reading Ease scores, indicating better patient accessibility, whereas Grok 4 produced more complex texts requiring higher educational levels.

evidence.title: [Evaluation of the efficacy of different large language models in solving clinical problems of early gastric cancer]
evidence.outcome: Readability (SMOG) of LLM answers to early gastric cancer patient questions and patient-rated comprehensibility
evidence.effect: SMOG scores were high: DeepSeek-V3.2 14.1±1.6, ChatGPT-4o 16.4±2.3, Gemini-2.5 15.8±2.0, Grok-3 15.8±1.1. Patient comprehensibility was 79.0 for DeepSeek-V3.2 vs 88.0 for ChatGPT-4o (P<0.05).
evidence.quote: In terms of readability assessment, the simple measure of gobbledygook (SMOG) score for DeepSeek-V3.2's responses (14.1±1.6) was lower than that of ChatGPT-4o (16.4±2.3), Gemini-2.5 (15.8±2.0) and Grok-3 (15.8±1.1) (all P<0.05).

evidence.title: Quality of AI chatbot-generated information on hypersensitivity pneumonitis for clinical and patient use
evidence.venue: Sarcoidosis, vasculitis, and diffuse lung diseases : official journal of WASOG
evidence.outcome: Readability (FKGL) of chatbot answers to patient questions about hypersensitivity pneumonitis
evidence.effect: FKGL ranged 20.17 to 29.07 (mean about 24-25, college/postgraduate level); no chatbot met the patient-appropriate FKGL of 8 or below. WRR fell from 67.85 (Q1) to 51.227 (Q4).
evidence.quote: No chatbot produced content within the recommended patient-appropriate range (FKGL ≤ 8).

evidence.title: Online Andrology: Real-World Status Quo of Patients' Online Information Sources and Comparison With Large Language Models in Germany
evidence.outcome: Comprehensibility and readability of LLM and website medical information for andrology patients (DISCERN, Flesch)
evidence.effect: Most common websites and LLMs gave sufficient information but lacked easy comprehensibility and readability.
evidence.quote: In general, most common websites and LLMs provide sufficient information but lack easy comprehensibility and readability.

evidence.title: Comparative evaluation of traditional versus generative AI patient education material on prehabilitation
evidence.outcome: Readability and understandability of AI-generated prehabilitation patient education versus NHS leaflet
evidence.effect: ChatGPT readability comparable to NHS leaflet; PEMAT-P understandability >75% for all materials; actionability highest for NHS (93.3%). Expert accuracy lower for all AI models than NHS (9.8 ± 0.3).
evidence.quote: For readability, ChatGPT and the National Health Service were comparable.
evidence.sample_unit: expert raters (4 patient education materials evaluated)

evidence.title: Evaluating chat generative pre-trained transformer responses to common patient questions on temporomandibular disorders
evidence.outcome: Readability grade level of ChatGPT responses on temporomandibular disorders
evidence.effect: Flesch-Kincaid grade 6.2-10.7 (mean 8.0), middle-to-high school comprehension; some responses above typical patient reading levels.
evidence.quote: Readability levels ranged from grade 6.2-10.7 (mean 8.0), corresponding to middle-to-high school comprehension.

evidence.title: Preclinical Dialogue Simulation: Evaluating Response Accessibility in Conversational Artificial Intelligence for Aphasia Therapy
evidence.venue: Journal of speech, language, and hearing research : JSLHR
evidence.outcome: Readability of LLM clinician language measured with Flesch Reading Ease, Dale-Chall and composite score
evidence.effect: LLMs differ systematically in adapting clinician language to impaired speech; accessibility depended on model, prompting, and reasoning mode.
evidence.quote: LLMs differ systematically in their capacity to adapt clinician language to impaired speech.

evidence.title: Performance of large language models in delivering accurate and comprehensible patient information on heart failure and cardiomyopathy
evidence.outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid grade level) of LLM responses to patient heart failure and cardiomyopathy questions
evidence.effect: Most readable model (Gemini) still scored Flesch-Kincaid Grade 11.3 ± 1.9 with 668.7 ± 116.1 words; linguistic complexity and length varied substantially across models.
evidence.quote: Gemini provided the most readable responses (Flesch-Kincaid Grade 11.3 ± 1.9) but was among the most verbose (668.7 ± 116.1 words).

evidence.title: A Cross-Sectional Study of Large Language Models in Lung Cancer Information Delivery: Readability, Quality, and Patient-Centred Evaluation
evidence.outcome: Readability (SMOG) and understandability/actionability (PEMAT-P) of LLM lung cancer answers
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-4o mini reached a sixth-grade level (SMOG 6.23 ± 0.72, p < 0.001) and highest PEMAT-P (63.7%); other models were less readable and all had moderate mDISCERN quality.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT-4o mini demonstrated superior readability, achieving a sixth-grade level (SMOG: 6.23 ± 0.72, p < 0.001).

evidence.title: Comparative Evaluation of ChatGPT-5.4 Mini and Gemini 3 Flash in Scar Patient Education: Quality, Reliability, and Readability Analysis
evidence.outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of AI-generated patient education responses
evidence.effect: Both models' readability thresholds were far above the 6th- to 8th-grade standard for patient education materials.
evidence.quote: Readability analysis showed that the reading thresholds of both models were excessively high, far exceeding the internationally recommended 6th- to 8th-grade standard for patient education materials.

evidence.title: Large Language Models for Breast and Cervical Cancers Communication: Mixed Methods Evaluation Study Assessing Linguistic Quality, Safety, and Accessibility
evidence.outcome: Readability and clarity of LLM breast and cervical cancer outputs
evidence.effect: General-purpose LLMs (Llama 3, Gemma) gave high-quality but often complex outputs that may limit accessibility. Medical LLMs (MedAlpaca, BioMistral) gave simpler content suited to broader audiences.
evidence.quote: General-purpose LLMs, particularly Llama 3 and Gemma, demonstrated superior linguistic quality and affectiveness but often produced complex outputs that may limit accessibility.

evidence.title: Assessing The Ability of ChatGPT 5.2 to Answer Patient Questions Regarding Hip Avascular Necrosis
evidence.outcome: Readability (FRES, FKRL) of ChatGPT 5.2 answers to patient questions about hip AVN
evidence.effect: Mean FRES 27.1 (range 12.4-45.6), 'difficult to read'; FKRL corresponded to college or college graduate reading levels.
evidence.quote: The mean FRES score was 27.1 (range: 12.4-45.6), indicating the content was "difficult to read."

evidence.title: Gonarthrosis Advisor vs ChatGPT-5: quality and readability of artificial intelligence-generated patient education for knee osteoarthritis
evidence.outcome: Readability of AI-generated knee osteoarthritis patient education (FKGL, FRES, Ateşman, Çakır-Demir)
evidence.effect: ChatGPT-5 FKGL 9.6 ± 0.9 vs Gonarthrosis Advisor 7.8 ± 0.7; FRES 46.7 vs 54.3; both above plain-language grade targets, guideline-tuned model better (all P<.001)
evidence.quote: Readability metrics favored the Gonarthrosis Advisor across all indices: lower FKGL (7.8 ± 0.7 vs. 9.6 ± 0.9) and higher FRES (54.3 ± 3.4 vs. 46.7 ± 3.7), Ateşman (92.0 ± 4.2 vs. 84.3 ± 4.9), and Çakır-Demir (111.7 ± 5.1 vs. 106.9 ± 5.4) scores (all P <.001).

evidence.title: Readability and Quality of Chatbot Responses to Periodontal Patient Queries: A Cross-Sectional Evaluation of Three Publicly Accessible Large Language Models
evidence.outcome: Readability (FRE, FKGL) of LLM responses to periodontal patient questions
evidence.effect: FKGL differed by model (p=0.007); ChatGPT-4o 11.18 ± 1.55, DeepSeek-R1 9.84 ± 1.78, Gemini 9.91 ± 1.89. FRE scores 42.37-49.55, all in the "difficult" range.
evidence.quote: All evaluated LLMs produced responses with mean QAMAI scores at the lower end of the predefined good-quality range; however, their readability exceeded recommended standards for public health materials.

evidence.title: Performance and usability of retrieval-augmented large language models for stroke patient and caregiver support
evidence.outcome: Understandability of LLM responses for patients with RAG versus zero-shot
evidence.effect: Adding RAG slightly reduced understandability for Claude3.7 and Qwen3.
evidence.quote: However, the addition of RAG slightly reduced understandability for Claude3.7 and Qwen3.
evidence.sample_unit: exam questions (plus 30 open-ended questions rated by 3 clinicians; usability testing with 20 stroke survivors and caregivers)

evidence.title: Assessment of the Accuracy and Readability of Artificial Generative Intelligence for Patient Questions on Heavy Menstrual Bleeding
evidence.venue: Journal of obstetrics and gynaecology Canada : JOGC = Journal d'obstetrique et gynecologie du Canada : JOGC
evidence.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading grade level of AI responses versus web-based patient resources
evidence.effect: AI responses written at lower grade level (7.6 ± 2.4) than web-based excerpts (11.1 ± 5.2; P = 0.042), without impacting content quality.
evidence.quote: Without impacting content quality, AI responses were written at a lower grade level (7.6 ± 2.4) than web-based excerpts (11.1 ± 5.2; P = 0.042).

evidence.title: Performance of large language models in mitral valve surgery patient education: a comparative analysis
evidence.venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
evidence.outcome: Readability (SMOG, FKGL) of LLM answers to mitral valve surgery patient questions
evidence.effect: SMOG 10.90 (Claude 3.7 Sonnet) vs 12.24 (ChatGPT-4o), p=0.006; FKGL 8.0 vs 9.04, p=0.004. Even the most readable model scored at about an 8th-grade level or above.
evidence.quote: Claude 3.7 Sonnet achieved the highest readability scores, with significantly lower SMOG (10.90 for Claude 3.7 Sonnet vs. 12.24 for ChatGPT-4o, p = 0.006) and FKGL (8.0 for Claude 3.7 Sonnet vs. 9.04 for ChatGPT-4o, p = 0.004) scores, indicating simpler and more comprehensible sentence structures.

evidence.title: Accuracy of an artificial intelligence chatbot in identifying congenital glaucoma from other ocular etiologies
evidence.outcome: Readability (SMOG index) of ChatGPT responses about congenital glaucoma
evidence.effect: SMOG Index was 14.8 ± 1.2 for ChatGPT-4.0 vs 14.0 ± 1.4 for ChatGPT-3.5 (P = 0.009), indicating college-level reading difficulty.
evidence.quote: Among readability indices, the SMOG Index score showed more difficult readability scores for ChatGPT-4.0 than for ChatGPT-3.5 (14.8 ± 1.2 vs 14.0 ± 1.4 [P = 0.009]).
evidence.sample_unit: text prompts (33 per model) plus 3 clinical images

evidence.title: Performance of large language models as an information resource on functional hypothalamic amenorrhea for patients and healthcare professionals
evidence.outcome: Flesch Reading Ease of LLM patient-level responses on FHA
evidence.effect: Median FRES was 43.5 (IQR 36.8-53.4) for Gemini, 30.6 (16.8-48.4) for ChatGPT 3.5, and 28.8 (22.1-37.6) for ChatGPT 4.0; lower scores indicate more difficult reading.
evidence.quote: Readability differed significantly among models (p = 0.012), with Gemini producing the most readable patient-level content (median FRES 43.5 [IQR 36.8-53.4]) compared with ChatGPT 3.5 (30.6 [16.8-48.4]) and ChatGPT 4.0 (28.8 [22.1-37.6]).

evidence.title: Large language model chatbots as sources of pediatric anesthesia health advice: An evaluation of reliability and readability
evidence.outcome: Readability of chatbot pediatric anesthesia responses versus recommended sixth-grade level across seven indices
evidence.effect: None of the four chatbots achieved the recommended sixth-grade readability level on any of the seven readability indices; reliability and readability correlations were non-significant.
evidence.quote: None of the evaluated models achieved the recommended sixth-grade readability level across any index.

evidence.title: Readability, Quality, Understandability, and Actionability of ChatGPT Generated GI Patient Education Versus AGA Patient Center
evidence.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading grade level of ChatGPT vs AGA patient education materials
evidence.effect: Mean FKGL was higher for ChatGPT than GI website materials (10.33 ± 1.5 vs 8.72 ± 1.7; mean difference 1.61; P < .001).
evidence.quote: The mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level was higher for ChatGPT than GI website materials (10.33 ± 1.5 vs 8.72 ± 1.7; mean difference, 1.61; P < .001).

evidence.title: Readability and Linguistic Characteristics of Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias Prevention, Symptom, and Treatment Information from Generative Artificial Intelligence Chatbots
evidence.outcome: Readability grade level of ADRD information from GenAI chatbots
evidence.effect: ADRD information from GenAI chatbots, especially treatment information, had college-level readability, exceeding recommended reading levels for patient education materials.
evidence.quote: Our sample of ADRD GenAI information exceeded recommended reading levels for patient education materials.

evidence.title: Development of a human-artificial intelligence collaboration-based storybook series for understanding epilepsy and supporting self-management
evidence.outcome: Expert-rated understandability and actionability of AI-generated epilepsy storybooks (PEMAT-A/V) and reliability (DISCERN)
evidence.effect: Mean DISCERN 71.03 ± 1.09; PEMAT-A/V understandability/applicability scores of 92.22 and 100, rated by five experts.
evidence.quote: Results showed high reliability (mean DISCERN score = 71.03 ± 1.09) and excellent understandability and applicability (PEMAT-A/V scores of 92.22 and 100).

evidence.title: Assessing Readability and DISCERN Quality of Osteoporosis Education Materials Generated by ChatGPT and Deepseek for Diverse Health Literacy Levels: A Cross-Sectional Study
evidence.outcome: Plain-language readability of AI-generated patient education across literacy tiers
evidence.effect: Three of four models met FKGL ≤ 8 for low literacy; ChatGPT-4o produced FKGL 10.37 for low tier; moderate-tier texts of three models were about 9th grade (FKGL 9.01–9.23).

evidence.title: Reliability and readability of adenoid hypertrophy information generated by five publicly accessible LLM chatbots: A default-setting snapshot study
evidence.outcome: Readability of chatbot responses on adenoid hypertrophy versus recommended sixth-grade level
evidence.effect: No model met the recommended sixth-grade reading level; Gemini best (FRES 61.95±9.64), Copilot poorest (FRES 24.27±10.77); P<0.001.
evidence.quote: All models failed to meet the recommended sixth-grade readability thresholds.

evidence.title: Supporting patient understanding of cervical and ovarian cancer: how well does AI perform?
evidence.outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient-facing answers relative to average American reading level
evidence.effect: All chatbot responses were above 11th grade reading level, generally difficult for the average American to read.
evidence.quote: All AI chatbot responses were written at a reading level above 11th grade, making them generally difficult for the average American to read.
evidence.sample_unit: questions (15 cervical, 11 ovarian cancer FAQs) posed to each of five chatbots

evidence.title: Artificial intelligence-based patient information in rotator cuff injuries: A cross-sectional comparative study of ChatGPT and DeepSeek models
evidence.outcome: Readability of AI patient education responses (FRES, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level)
evidence.effect: Both models showed similar readability (FRES P >.05; FKGL P >.05); authors conclude readability requires improvement.
evidence.quote: However, they require improvements in terms of adherence to scientific standards, transparency, citations, and readability.

evidence.title: A Comparative Cross-sectional Study Assessing the Readability of ChatGPT and UpToDate Content on Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Syndromes
evidence.outcome: Readability (FRE, FKGL) of ChatGPT-generated MEN patient education text versus UpToDate
evidence.effect: ChatGPT FRE 21.3 and FKGL 15.3; UpToDate FRE 24.9 and FKGL 16.7; both above suggested readability limits for patient materials.
evidence.quote: Both sources scored poorly in readability: ChatGPT had an FRE of 21.3 and FKGL of 15.3, while UTD scored 24.9 and 16.7, respectively.

evidence.title: Large language model based simplification of ophthalmological clinical and ancillary results for patient readability
evidence.venue: International journal of retina and vitreous
evidence.outcome: Readability grade level of original ophthalmological reports versus patient reading level
evidence.effect: Original reports median aRGL 13.8 overall, 11.6 for fundus, 15.4 for ocular ultrasound; LLMs improved readability, with the 7th-grade prompt best.
evidence.quote: The original reports were highly complex, with a median aRGL of 13.8 overall, 11.6 for fundus reports, and 15.4 for ocular ultrasound reports.

evidence.title: Fine-Tuning, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, and Hybrid Large Language Models for Postoperative Decision Support: Comparative Analysis
evidence.outcome: Readability of AI-generated postoperative patient education outputs relative to recommended reading levels
evidence.effect: Enhanced models had FKGL 10.6-11.8 and lower FRE (35.1-40.0), exceeding AMA/NIH 6th-8th grade recommendations; baseline FKGL 9.7 also above.
evidence.quote: Although the enhanced models, particularly the hybrid configuration, achieved the highest accuracy, they also generated responses exceeding AMA and NIH-recommended patient education reading levels (sixth to eighth grade level) [ 39 ].

evidence.title: Clinician-supervised large language AI model after-discharge instruction generation for common emergency department presentations
evidence.outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of LLM discharge instructions for marginalised patient personas
evidence.effect: Persona reviews revealed persistent medical jargon and vague instructions that could hinder understanding for marginalised groups.
evidence.quote: Whilst Claude was preferred for simpler language after revisions, persona reviews revealed persistent medical jargon and vague instructions that could hinder understanding for marginalised groups.

evidence.title: Assessing Quality, Readability, and Transparency of Online and AI-Generated Information on Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Cross-Sectional Exploratory Study
evidence.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading grade level of AI-generated type 2 diabetes patient leaflets

evidence.quote: Mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level scores for websites were 8.67 (SD 2.23) and 8.30 (SD 1.92) for AIGLs, corresponding to an eighth- to ninth-grade comprehension level.

evidence.title: ChatGPT-5.4 in health education: inter-generation stability and persistent readability challenges

evidence.quote: Readability remains above recommended health- literacy levels, and clinician review and plain-language optimization are required before patient use.

evidence.title: Assessing retina-specific ophthalmic counseling generated by an early public large language model across different levels of clinical urgency
evidence.outcome: Readability of LLM counseling outputs by readability indices

evidence.quote: Four readability indices (e.g., Flesch Kincaid Grade Level) consistently indicated that college graduation would be required to understand every counseling output.

evidence.title: Artificial Intelligence Large Language Models for Pelvic Floor Rehabilitation: Readabilty, Usability and Consistency
evidence.outcome: Readability of LLM answers (FRE, FKRGL, SMOG) for pelvic floor rehabilitation questions
evidence.effect: Significant SMOG differences among models at both evaluations (p<0.001), and for FKGL at the second evaluation only (p=0.006). Authors concluded that the answers were readable.
evidence.quote: ChatGPT, DeepSeek and Gemini provided readable, useful and repeatable answers to questions related to pelvic floor rehabilitation.

evidence.title: Evaluation of the performance and temporal variability of large language models in patient education regarding pneumothorax: a seven-day analysis
evidence.outcome: readability of patient education outputs
evidence.effect: Unprompted configurations consistently generated complex, high-school-level outputs; PROMPORT compressed linguistic variances and neutralized drift (p > 0.05).
evidence.quote: Unprompted configurations consistently generated complex, high-school-level outputs, whereas the PROMPORT strategy successfully compressed linguistic variances and neutralized chronological algorithmic drift (p > 0.05).

evidence.title: Evaluating the quality, understandability, actionability, and readability of ChatGPT-generated patient information on overactive bladder: A cross-sectional study
evidence.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT-4o OAB patient information (FKGL, SMOG) versus recommended patient education standards
evidence.effect: Responses exceeded recommended standards; overall median FKGL 14.00 (range 7.61-17.11) and SMOG 12.34 (range 5.01-14.93).

evidence.title: Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence Communication Platform for Racial Biases in Pretest Education About Prostate Cancer Germline Testing
evidence.outcome: Readability grade level of chatbot patient education responses
evidence.effect: Mean readability was 10th grade (SMOG) and 13th grade (Flesch-Kincaid); none varied by race.

evidence.title: Quality of AI-generated exercise awareness messages for older adults aligned with the ICFSR consensus: a comparative study of three LLMs

evidence.outcome: Readability (FKGL, GFI, SMOG) of LLM messages versus recommended level for older adults

evidence.title: LLM-Generated Lay-Language Protocols for Molecular Tumor Board Patients: Evaluation of Quality and Clinical Usability
evidence.outcome: Readability and complexity of LLM-generated patient protocols versus expert-written gold standard
evidence.effect: WSTF4 remained in the medium difficulty range (10-12), about grade 10 or higher. DistilBERT complexity was 4.10-4.78 versus 2.79 for the gold standard.
evidence.quote: DistilBERT-based complexity assessments showed that all generated texts remained far from the gold standard (2.79) within a similar complexity range (4.10‐4.78), with no systematic differences between the approaches.

evidence.title: Comprehensive Evaluation of AI Consent Forms in Otolaryngologic Surgery

evidence.outcome: Readability (FKGL) of AI-generated consent forms versus official templates and target reading level

evidence.title: Using Large Language Models to Generate Retina Patient Education Material: A Comparative Analysis With American Society of Retina Specialists Patient Brochures

evidence.effect: Average readability was 14.17 for ASRS brochures and 11.23-12.85 for LLM materials, all well above sixth-grade level.

evidence.title: LLMs in Medical Education for Autism Caregivers: A Comparative Evaluation of Accuracy, Readability, Actionability, and Neurodiversity-Affirming Language
evidence.outcome: Readability (FKGL, SMOG) and actionability of LLM answers for autism caregivers versus patient education benchmarks

evidence.quote: Importantly, all models failed to meet established consumer education standards for readability and actionability.

evidence.title: A comparative analysis of readability, quality, and reliability in large language model outputs pertaining to knee osteoarthritis queries
evidence.outcome: Comprehensibility of AI chatbot patient information relative to recommended reading level
evidence.effect: Responses from all chatbots consistently exceeded the recommended comprehensibility threshold, making it difficult for patients to absorb information.

evidence.title: Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence Language Model for Generating Informed Consent Forms in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery: A QUEST Framework Analysis

evidence.outcome: Grade-level readability of AI-generated informed consent drafts
evidence.effect: Readability scores ranged from grade 6.0 to 8.0 (mean 6.85 ± 0.85), described as acceptable readability.
evidence.quote: Readability scores ranged from grade 6.0 to 8.0 (mean 6.85 ± 0.85).

evidence.title: Large Language Models for Individualized Psychoeducational Tools for Psychosis: A Cross-Sectional Study
evidence.outcome: Reading grade level (Flesch-Kincaid) of GPT-4 psychoeducational responses
evidence.effect: Mean FKGL 15.59 ± 1.59, indicating increased reading complexity for patients, caregivers and relatives.

evidence.title: Accuracy and Readability of Generative Artificial Intelligence for Vascular Surgery Patients: A Specialist Based Evaluation Highlighting the Current Landscape of Safety Risks and Accessibility Gaps
evidence.venue: European journal of vascular and endovascular surgery : the official journal of the European Society for Vascular Surgery

evidence.title: Can AI answer my questions? Using Artificial Intelligence to help provide information for patients with a stoma

evidence.title: Bridging the Gap in Health Literacy: Harnessing the Power of Large Language Models to Generate Plain Language Summaries from Biomedical Texts

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT on Orbital and Oculofacial Disorders: Accuracy and Readability Insights
evidence.outcome: Reading level of ChatGPT responses on orbital and oculofacial disease

evidence.title: Evaluating ChatGPT Responses on Thyroid Nodules for Patient Education

evidence.title: An artificial intelligence language model improves readability of burns first aid information

commentary.bottom_line: Randomized trials in real deployments suggest that plain-language AI versions of radiology and other reports improve patient comprehension, though a large simulated trial found no gain in tested comprehension. Simplified outputs often miss sixth-grade reading targets and sometimes drop content, so review for accuracy and completeness may be needed.

perspectives.view: Three randomized trials in real deployments, with 64 to 120 patients each, found that simplified reports raised patient comprehension; one reported quiz scores of 74.7% vs 54.7%. A fourth trial found clinician diagnostic understanding rose 9.0 points. A simulated trial of 2727 participants found no difference in objective comprehension (58.3% vs 59.4%). Small samples and inconsistency limit certainty to moderate.

Simplification may drop content. In one offline study a plain-language prompt lowered DISCERN treatment-information scores by 11.58 and 11.00 points and reduced completeness, and in another comprehensiveness ratings fell from 3.91 to 3.68. Tested comprehension of normal MRI reports fell from 76.6% to 72.5% with lay summaries. A cardiologist found none of 143 revised materials less accurate.

Automated simplification often misses target reading levels. Only 14 of 86 revised education materials and 2 of 25 simplified answers reached sixth-grade level. In routine use, 4 of 982 AI visit summaries met a sixth-grade benchmark, which documents the problem rather than testing a fix. One chatbot study found technical language produced larger knowledge gains (OR 2.73).

In a pre-post study of 698 pathology reports, doctor-patient communication time fell from 35 to 10 minutes with plain-language interpretations. A quasi-experimental study found median patient reading time fell from 7 to 2 minutes. Neither study reports cost, and no study measures the staff time needed to review simplified outputs before release.

A study in China with non-English-speaking patients found that simplified language and standardized formatting improved clarity (adjusted P=.02). An offline study of heart failure materials for low health literacy readers found median grade level fell from 10th to 7th. In a minority-focused survey, 35.0% of chatbot users reported they could not fully understand responses.

Patients favored plain-language versions, and 87.5% preferred an AI translation of their MRI report. In the large simulated trial, satisfaction and self-rated comprehension rose while tested comprehension did not change. In a hazard study, 83-90% of patients rated chatbot text as clear although it exceeded recommended reading levels. Self-reported clarity may overstate understanding.

commentary.research_gap: No trial measured downstream outcomes such as medication errors, follow-up adherence, or treatment decisions after patients read simplified outputs, and only one randomized trial tested clinician-facing summaries. Most trials examined radiology reports, so evidence for patient education materials and chatbot outputs rests on offline readability studies. Trials that pair objective comprehension with content-omission endpoints, and that compare clinician-reviewed with unreviewed simplification, are needed.
commentary.underserved_note: None of the randomized trials that tested plain-language simplification reported enrolling Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy patients. Among tests of the practice, three smaller or offline studies involved non-English or low health literacy contexts (pmid:42464799, epmc:PPR1312893, epmc:PPR937748), and two of them measured readability or rated clarity rather than tested comprehension. Two randomized studies that enrolled limited English or non-English patients (pmid:40162329, pmid:42425711) documented hard-to-read chatbot output but did not test simplification as a remedy. The comprehension gains seen in trials may therefore not carry over to patients with limited literacy or limited English.
